This game has a serious problem: it keeps adding complexity instead of improving the actual experience.

Everything feels unnecessarily bloated. The UI, the gameplay mechanics, the customization options—every system seems designed to overwhelm the player rather than make the game more enjoyable. There are more features than ever, yet the core gameplay feels worse.

Passing feels stiff and unnatural. The ball often follows rigid trajectories that make it feel disconnected from what's happening on the pitch.
Player movement is harder to control than before, but not in a realistic or rewarding way. It simply feels less responsive and more frustrating.
The AI customization system is packed with options, yet most of them have little noticeable impact. Players are expected to spend time tweaking countless settings for results that barely justify the effort.

What makes this even more frustrating is the lack of a clear direction. Why not simply offer two distinct gameplay styles: Assisted and Manual? If you want accessibility, fully commit to Assisted controls. If you want skill-based gameplay, fully commit to Manual controls. Instead, the game sits awkwardly in the middle, creating a confusing half-assisted, half-manual experience that adds complexity without adding depth.

It feels like the developers are solving problems nobody asked them to solve while ignoring the issues that actually matter: responsiveness, fluid gameplay, and intuitive controls.

The end result isn't a deeper football simulation. It's a more frustrating one.

EA Sports FC 26 Review: The Ultimate $70 Roster Update & Microtransaction SimulatorScore: 1.5 / 10Verdict: EA has somehow outdone themselves, creating a game that feels less like a sport and more like a high-stress slot machine wrapped in bad netcode.Gameplay: Ice Skates & Broken PhysicsIf you enjoyed the fast-paced, fluid tactical play of real-world football, stay as far away from FC 26 as possible. Every match feels like playing a game of pinball on ice.The AI is Unhinged: Your defensive line acts like it's never seen a football before. AI defenders routinely mark invisible ghost players, step out of position to let pace-demons run straight past them, or stand around like traffic cones.The "Scripting" Experience: The DDA (Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment) has reached peak comedy. You can be leading 3–0 in the 80th minute, only for your 90+ rated squad to suddenly move like they are swimming in wet cement while your opponent's bronze card striker morphs into Prime Lionel Messi.  Goalkeepers: They either save 15 impossible point-blank shots in a row or dive away from a slow, rolling ball. There is no middle ground.Ultimate Team: Pay-to-Win Has EvolvedEA's priority is painfully obvious within five minutes of launching the game: your checkbook."It’s not a football simulation; it’s a lootbox casino that occasionally lets you play 20 minutes of FIFA between opening packs."The push for microtransactions is more aggressive than ever. Store packs cost a fortune, the Season Pass locks core rewards behind paywalls, and the power creep is so fast that the team you worked hard for last week is completely obsolete by Friday. If you aren't spending real money, prepare to spend your weekends getting stomped by credit card FC in Weekend League.  Career Mode & Clubs: Abandoned AgainFor the offline players and the Pro Clubs enthusiasts, FC 26 is a masterclass in copy-pasting code.Career Mode: Still plagued by the same menu bugs, absurd transfer logic (why is AI Real Madrid buying five right-backs?), and lifeless cutscenes that haven't changed in years.Pro Clubs: Server disconnections, broken matchmaking, and AI teammates that pass directly to the enemy team.The VerdictEA Sports FC 26 proves once again that without any real competition in the market, EA doesn't need to make a good football game—they just need to make a functional store page. Save your money, save your sanity, and stick to playing the older games or literally anything else.

I haven't bought a FIFA game—or any EA game at all—since FIFA 20. After a six-year break I decided to give EA Sports FC 26 a chance when it recently went on sale for €14. Even at a massive discount, I regret buying it and am actively looking into a refund.
To be clear about my perspective: I do not play Ultimate Team. I have zero interest in opening card packs, gambling with loot boxes, or throwing real money at EA. Unacceptable Server Lag & Stability: I play on a high-speed Fiber Optic connection. Every other competitive online game I play runs flawlessly with zero latency issues. FC 26, on the other hand, is a laggy, stuttering nightmare.

Verdict: I paid €14 just to play basic online divisions and couch co-op, and it still feels like a total waste of money. EA’s priorities remain entirely displaced, favoring microtransactions over a functional video game. I will continue to boycott EA Sports titles

[h1] Offline Career Mode Enjoyer Review [/h1]

[b] No, I don't play Ultimate Team. [/b]
[b] No, I don't open packs. [/b]
[b] No, I don't care about your Mbappé card with +1 Pace. [/b]

I only play [b] Manager Career[/b] and [b] Player Career[/b], so this review is for people who actually enjoy pretending they're managing a football club.

[h3] This is my first FIFA/EA FC game. Looking at older titles and the upcoming FC 27, I've come to one conclusion:  [/h3]

• EA has been selling the same sandwich with a slightly different wrapper for years.

• Launching the game is the first boss fight.
Sometimes the game launches.
Sometimes it doesn't.
Sometimes I launch it three times because the EA App decides today isn't a football day.

• When it finally works, does it let me play?
Of course not. First, here's a giant preorder ad for the next game.
Then several windows telling me to connect to EA servers.
Brother... I'm playing offline Career Mode.
I don't care if the servers are on fire.

[h3] Performance? [/h3]

• The famous FPS drops after cutscenes?
Yep. Had those too.
The good news is I fixed them.
The bad news is... [i]fixed them.[/i]
Apparently the community deserves part of EA's paycheck because they're doing customer support for free.

[h3] Player Career has the memory of a goldfish. [/h3]

• The social media feature exists because... reasons.
The posts are repetitive, awkward, and sometime unmatch.

• The opening and second cutscenes make you think you're about to experience your player's journey.
Plot twist:
That [i] was[/i] the journey.
After that, your character basically communicates with the world through recycled tweets and facial expressions.

• The ending is comedy.
After spending [b] 15 seasons [/b] building my player's legacy...
No retirement match.
No news about me.
No farewell speech.
The game simply says:
"Cool. Which club do you want to manage?"
That's it.


[h3] Despite all of that... [/h3]

I've played almost [b] 300 hours. [/b]

Because underneath all the launcher issues, advertisements, server pop-ups, half-finished features, and questionable design decisions... Career Mode is still fun enough to make me come back because of the gameplay and movement.

[h3] Verdict [/h3]

✔ Free? Absolutely.
✔ 90% off? Easy recommendation.
✘ Full price? I'd rather spend that money to somewhere else than funding another Jude Bellingham photoshoot.

[b] Recommended for:[/b] Offline Career Mode addicts who can tolerate EA's nonsense.[b] Not recommended for:[/b]  Anyone expecting a polished AAA experience from a company that somehow made launching the game and fixing the bugs is more difficult than winning the Champions League.

**Inconsistent, buggy and not worth the full price**

EA SPORTS FC 26 can be enjoyable when it actually works, but the experience is far too inconsistent to recommend at its current price.

The game is filled with bugs, and frustratingly, new updates often seem to introduce even more problems rather than fixing what is already broken. Since the latest update, I have experienced scouts not carrying out their assignments properly and stadium audio randomly disappearing, including crowd atmosphere and commentary. These issues make Career Mode and matches feel unfinished and lifeless.

Gameplay is equally inconsistent. One match can feel responsive and enjoyable, while the next feels slow, unresponsive and completely different. Passing, defending, player movement and AI behaviour regularly change without any obvious reason.

The biggest shame is that FC 26 has some genuinely good mechanics and creative ideas, particularly within Manager Career Mode. There is the foundation of a very good football game here, and at times it can be engaging and enjoyable. Unfortunately, the constant bugs, inconsistent gameplay and unreliable updates prevent those good ideas from reaching their potential.

For a full-priced annual release from a company with this much experience and money behind it, FC 26 should be far more polished and consistent. It simply is not worth the asking price in its current condition.

I would recommend waiting for a substantial sale rather than paying full price.

Okay, so, obviously a lot of people aren't happy with this game... I don't, and have never, and will never play Ultimate Team. I don't play online (though I will if any of my friends want to play), so all of that stuff is irrelevant to me.
I primarily like to play a manager career. My approach to the game is picking a sub-top flight squad (my typical starting point is Birmingham City), using the youth academy & transfer market to bring in a squad of young players with a lot of potential, and carrying my team to the tippy-top.

Previous FIFA/FC games, I've played comfortably at World Class difficulty. Since I was out of touch, having been a couple of years since I've really played, I started up on Professional. It only took a few matches until I was warmed up enough to be winning every game easily with a 7+ goal advantage. So, naturally, I upped to World Class.
Here is where I had an issue with this game...
Professional - 10-0 every game, World Class - I can't even touch the ball. 
I don't know what this is about, but it was very frustrating. I tried moving the sliders around to improve things, but it didn't get much better. 
I've spent the last few weeks playing on Professional with CPU sliders increased dramatically. This, I feel, is far closer to what I remember World Class difficulty being. But now that I've completed two seasons with these settings, I'm going to try World Class again. We'll see how that goes.

There is also a really annoying graphical glitch that will render players/managers hair the wrong color during celebrations etc.
& When you play a youth tournament (Rush match), the music gets set to 'always ON', and you have to manually turn it off afterwards.
The commentators are pretty bad, also. The classic commentary teams are gone, and what we have now just feels very generic and lacking. 
I also am not a fan of how they've allowed gender neutral refereeing... Women don't referee men's games in real life, so why do they here?

I've been waiting a decade for EA to improve upon the actual engine - they change mechanics, and movement/inputs are improved upon, but I feel like we're still seeing the same graphics/animations that we've been looking at for 15 years.
Hardware has evolved - we can handle some better graphics! 

Other than that, I have no real complaints with the game.
The gameplay has improved over previous entries - they've changed some of the modifying controls for shot/pass types, which took me a minute to get used to, but everything feels pretty smooth and intuitive. 
The game runs flawlessly - little to no loading times.
I'm having the same experience that I've had with these titles for years. It's still as much fun as it always has been. 
I've been playing EA football games since FIFA 94 on the SEGA Mega Drive, and I don't know if I'll ever stop... However, as I have done in recent years, I WILL delay my purchase of a title until a decent sale price shows up, UNTIL they upgrade the engine. I want to see revolutionary graphics and animations. Not polished versions of the same thing I've been looking at for half of my life. 

Thank you for your attention in this matter

Every year, sports fans brace themselves for another round of promises from annual game updates. Tighter gameplay, smarter AI, deeper modes, all wrapped in another sleek package that does just enough to justify the price of admission. Most years, the actual results fall somewhere between ‘incremental’ and ‘wow.’ Unfortunately, EA Sports FC 26 lands squarely on the lower end of that spectrum this season, bringing users a competent entry that shows a modicum of improvement on top of a core experience that still feels frustratingly inconsistent.

When I first loaded FC 26, I expected more of the same — refined controls, another minor Career mode adjustment, and a handful of Ultimate Team tweaks. As it turns out, that’s essentially what I got, though not in ways that reliably improves the experience.

The biggest change is the addition of two distinct gameplay presets — Competitive and Authentic.

Competitive mode caters to the online crowd, and is designed for the fast, responsive pace of FUT and Clubs. I found more enjoyment using Authentic mode, which slows the tempo, adding more weight and realism to each movement. In this setting, defenders more accurately hold their positions, midfielders fight for spacing, and goals feel earned, rather than expected. It’s a split that acknowledges how different the FC audience can be, but it also feels like EA is hedging its bets, rather than committing to a cohesive vision

Football is more than just a sport, and EA SPORTS FC™ 26 does a fantastic job of bringing that feeling onto the pitch. Whether you're scoring a last-minute winner in Career Mode, dominating your friends in Kick-Off, or building your dream squad, every match feels exciting and rewarding.

The gameplay is the biggest improvement this year. Dribbling feels smoother, passing is more responsive, defenders position themselves intelligently, and goalkeepers finally make realistic saves instead of acting unpredictably. The addition of Competitive and Authentic gameplay presets lets you choose between fast-paced online action and a more realistic football simulation, making every mode feel unique.

Career Mode remains my favorite part of the game. Building a club from scratch, signing young talents, developing players, managing transfers, creating tactics, and chasing league titles never gets old. The new Manager Live Challenges and improved tactical systems make every season feel more dynamic instead of repetitive.

Player Career is also more enjoyable thanks to better progression, Archetypes, PlayStyles, and Player Roles that let you create a footballer with a unique identity rather than just increasing overall ratings.

Visually, FC 26 looks fantastic. Stadiums are packed with life, player faces are highly detailed, lighting is beautiful, and match-day presentations feel incredibly authentic. Crowd chants, commentary, celebrations, and atmosphere combine to create a true football broadcast experience.

There is plenty of content for every type of player:

* ⚽ Career Mode
* 🌍 International tournaments
* 🎮 Clubs
* 🏆 Ultimate Team
* 👥 Online Seasons
* 🎯 Skill Games
* 🤝 Local & Online Multiplayer

The controls are easy to learn but difficult to master. Smart passing, precise finishing, tactical defending, and creative dribbling reward skill instead of button mashing, making every victory satisfying.

Like every EA football title, it isn't perfect. Server issues can occasionally appear during online play, Ultimate Team still encourages spending for faster progress, and yearly releases naturally don't reinvent the entire franchise. However, the gameplay improvements are noticeable enough that FC 26 feels far more polished than simply being a roster update.

## Pros

✔ Smooth and responsive gameplay
✔ Excellent graphics and stadium atmosphere
✔ Improved AI and goalkeeper behavior
✔ Deep and enjoyable Career Mode
✔ Great player progression and customization
✔ Massive selection of licensed clubs, leagues, and players
✔ Fun both offline and online

## Cons

✘ Ultimate Team can become pay-to-progress
✘ Occasional online server issues
✘ Annual releases still leave room for bigger innovation

 Final Verdict

EA SPORTS FC™ 26 successfully captures the excitement, pressure, and passion of real football. Whether you're a casual player looking to enjoy a few matches or someone who spends hundreds of hours building the perfect squad, there's always another trophy to chase, another wonderkid to sign, or another unforgettable goal to score.

Overall Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ 8/10

EA Sports FC 26 has some of the most frustrating gameplay I've experienced in the series, and the biggest reasons are the passing system and AI defending.

The passing feels wildly inconsistent. One minute, a simple five-yard pass goes exactly where you want it, and the next, your player ignores the obvious option and sends the ball to a completely different teammate. Through balls are just as unreliable, often being either massively overhit or underpowered, making even basic build-up play feel like a gamble instead of a skill. Rather than rewarding good vision and timing, the game frequently feels like it's fighting against your inputs. While EA has said it aimed to make passing more responsive, many players continue to report inconsistent pass targeting and accuracy.

AI defending is somehow even worse. Defenders constantly lose their shape, fail to track obvious runs, and stand around watching attackers instead of applying pressure. There are countless moments where center-backs simply back away from the ball carrier, leaving huge gaps that make defending feel completely unrealistic. Even when you manually position your defenders correctly, your AI teammates often refuse to help, making it feel like you're defending alone. Community feedback has been split, with some players arguing the AI is too passive while others complain it becomes overly automated after patches, highlighting how inconsistent the system feels.

The combination of poor passing and unreliable AI defending makes matches feel more random than rewarding. Instead of winning because you made the better decisions, it often feels like you're hoping the game's mechanics don't work against you. Every misplaced pass and every defender who forgets how to mark an attacker chips away at the enjoyment.

EA Sports FC 26 has flashes of potential, but until the passing becomes consistent and the AI defending behaves intelligently, it's difficult to recommend. Football games should reward skill, positioning, and smart decision-making—not leave players wondering whether the game will ignore their inputs on the next pass or let the defense fall apart for no reason.

Alright, real talk—as someone who sinks way too many hours into this series every year while swearing “never again,” FC 26 is the ultimate EA classic: the moment-to-moment football actually feels great, but the surrounding menus and monetization will still make you roll your eyes.

If you played FC 25, you’ll catch the difference in your first match. It’s not a brand-new game by any stretch, but the pitch gameplay is in a genuinely good spot.

The Stuff That Actually Works
Left-Stick Dribbling is Back: Controlling quick wingers or agile midfield agitates actually feels responsive again. The ball doesn't bounce five yards away when you take a turn, so you can actually weave through tight spaces.

Keepers Don't Throw Games (As Much): They finally patched out that infuriating habit where goalkeepers punch a soft shot directly to the open striker. They push parries wide and actually close down 1v1s with some intelligence.

The Gameplay Split Works: EA separated the tuning between modes. Authentic mode in Career Mode actually forces you to build up play and respect stamina, while Competitive mode keeps Ultimate Team fast, snappy, and end-to-end.

What Will Still Test Your Patience
"You can place a tackle perfectly, win the ball, and watch it bounce right back to the attacker three times in a row."

Tackling Logic: Because dribbling got a buff, manual defending feels like walking a tightrope. Miss a tackle by a millisecond and your defender gets trapped in a sluggish recovery animation while the winger breezes past.

Season Pass Creep: EA is pushing Battle Passes and premium reward tracks harder than ever. It used to just be an Ultimate Team thing, but now the menu design constantly tries to push you toward cosmetic unlocks and season progression, even if you just want a quick kick-off match.

Mode-by-Mode Snapshot
Career Mode: Surprisingly decent this year. The manager tactician options feel less gimmicky, and dynamic scenarios (like squad morale hits from sudden transfer rumors) keep seasons from feeling totally copy-pasted.

Ultimate Team: Fun on the pitch, exhausting off it. The gameplay loop is great early on, but you hit that pay-to-win or absurd-grind wall fast.

Clubs: Still the best reason to own the game. Drop in with a few mates, mess around with player builds, and just enjoy the chaos.

Bottom Line
If you're picking it up for Clubs with friends or a long-term Manager Career, it’s a genuine step up from FC 25 and well worth playing. But if you were hoping EA would tone down the microtransactions or magically fix defensive tackle rebounds, you already know the answer. Grab it on sale if you're on the fence, or dive in if your squad is already making the jump.

Last FIFA game I bought was FIFA 16. After that one, I said "NEVER AGAIN”. It's been 10 years since then. Many things around the franchise changed. But this year, I bought it because I saw a couple of friends playing it. I missed the feeling of building the Ultimate Team.

My verdict? I don’t think there is one single online game as broken as FC 26. Simply nothing about this game is even remotely functional. The game keeps throwing so much random sh*t at you which your mind could never have foreseen. There are so many things wrong with this game that I simply can’t address them all. And it’s barely football. It’s so arcadey, there is nothing realistic about this game.

I ABSOLUTELY DON’T RECOMMEND anyone to buy FC 27 after what FC 26 was.

FC 26 is one of the most unoptimized games I’ve ever touched. The game is even LAGGY IN THE MENUS, for God’s sake. I’ve had to disable all the bullsh*t cutscenes, in-background videos and overlays to make the menu barely usable. It is ridiculous, considering that you spend a good 50% of your playtime in the menu, especially in Ultimate Team. And it still randomly breaks, so you have to completely restart the game. And even then EA has the nerve to lock certain actions for UT behind their fu*king web companion. I hope you rot in hell.

Let’s talk about mechanics. They’re terrible. A lot of variation in mechanics, but they’re either completely broken or they don’t work at all.
Passing is awful. Tapping or holding the pass button makes absolutely no difference in 99% of cases. It will pass to the player you’re generally aiming at, with an emphasis on “generally”. For some reason, if two players are nearby, the game simply refuses to pass to the player that is not marked by an opponent. Passing within the box is HELL. I can’t even count the number of times I was on the edge of the box and wanted to pass to the center of the box, tapped the pass button and it sent the ball to the player on the CENTER OF THE FIELD. Through passes are absolutely disgusting, to the point where – 1. I don’t even use them unless it’s a 110% clear run through, or 2. I aim and power them fully manually. You send a player on the run, and the game still doesn’t acknowledge that that guy is the one you want to send a through pass to. Crosses are almost unusable, not because they don’t work, but because scoring a header in this game is next to impossible. Corner kicks are useless if you’re not calling for a player and passing it straight to him, because EVEN if you do get a header, and EVEN if it does go on target (which is very rare), and EVEN if it does go past the keeper, there are ALWAYS one or two players on the goal line that will get it out.
Switching is also terrible. There are no configurations that will make it work well. L1 switching is incredibly bad and unresponsive, and somehow, right stick switching is even worse. I’ve had countless occasions where I switch to defender, want to right stick switch to a center mid that is closer to the ball, and the game ends up switching on my striker that is at the center of the field. And then, while switching back to where you want, you’ve already conceded the goal.
I don’t hate the shooting mechanics. They’re versatile and they’re not overly complicated, you simply choose the preferred method you want to shoot with, press and hold. But what I do hate is that the goalkeepers are useless very often in this game for some reason. One game they’ll make normal saves, the next game, they’re dumb as rocks and they have the reflexes of a tree.

When it comes to matchmaking, it’s the biggest f*cking piece of sh*t I’ve ever seen. You simply have to play this game to understand just how badly rigged it is. I haven’t played a FIFA game in a long time, so I’ve had my doubts at first, but DDA (Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment) is REAL and it’s absolutely always there, not just in offline modes, but in online modes as well. Because there is no way that your defenders simply lack the pace sometimes and they randomly slow down because I know DAMN WELL that my defender and the opponent’s striker are equal on pace, equal on acceleration and equal on stamina, neither player has a physical Playstyle that gives them the extra boost, and my defender is still higher in strength. And sometimes it’s just pretty obvious with the way the players position themselves.
If you scored a goal, be sure that there is a very high chance that you might receive one straight from the kick-off. If you’re up 2-0 at half-time, be sure that there is a very high chance that you might lose the game in the second half. If you’re equal in the 45th+ or 90th+ minute of added time, be sure that there is a very high chance you will either score or concede a goal. These patterns occur so ridiculously often that there is not a single doubt in my mind that these matches are getting rigged or fixed. If you take these broken mechanics and add all the incredible randomness that occurs during a match, it adds up to one of the most frustrating, if not THE MOST FRUSTRATING experiences ever. And it’s a perfectly valid reason why I’m not buying this game again anytime soon.

And I won't even mention the number of cheaters in this game. EA FC is one of those rare games where I say, if you're going to buy this piece of sh*t, buy it on console.

AI difficulty is also really unbalanced. Professional level is very easy, and World Class, just one level above it, is sometimes unplayable. In Squad Battles, I regularly get raw dogged by 58-rated teams on Legendary, while I beat the 93-rated Featured Squad on Ultimate. I swear to God, these 58-rated teams move like prime Barca. It makes no sense.

Servers are also really terrible. Experiences vary from region to region, but the coverage is really bad. Some of my friends from Central Europe can’t play with friends from Eastern Europe, because the ping is horrendous.

Let’s address the Ultimate Team. If you’re not grinding day after day, you’re doomed. THERE HAVE BEEN MORE THAN 60 PROMOS IN FC 26. Let that sink in. FIFA 18 had 15, FIFA 22 had 23, FC 24 had 36. This one has 63 and counting at the time of this review. A card that is top-tier one week is mid-tier the next, and unusable a week after that. You could grind the game for a week and it wouldn’t even last a month. That is absolutely unacceptable, and I’m very glad that people are being loud about it.

And the other modes… I love Clubs, but the servers simply don’t work and you can never, ever, find a single damn match. Why the hell does it exist if I can’t go into a match with anyone? Career works better, because it's offline, but it has so many bugs that it's ridiculous. And there are a lot of cases where people's saves just get wiped with an update.
There are still no 2v2 online modes in the big 2026. Are you serious?

Next to that, EA Launcher is one of the worst things to exist. "EA Launcher can go to places where the sun doesn't shine." There are tons of people that simply can't start their own game, THAT THEY PAID FOR, because the launcher is broken and the EA Support can't even put 2 + 2 together.

I must mention that I’ve tried other football games before coming back to FC. Most notably eFootball. I like eFootball because it’s, in contrast to FC, more realistic in the way it’s paced. It’s simple, but sadly, it seems like a game nearing its death. And I find FC to be more fun in certain segments because it shows more variation, like the dribbling and skills.

Sadly, EA FC still doesn’t have real competitors. Because these cash-grabbing big*ts wouldn’t still be top sellers if there was anything remotely close.

EA Sports FC 26 is a frustratingly familiar entry in the annual football franchise that provides minor solitary enjoyment through its Player Career Mode, but ultimately fails to justify its existence due to recycled content. On the positive side, taking a custom pro or a real-world athlete through their professional journey remains an engaging loop, enhanced slightly by character archetypes. Taking a custom pro through a career path and building up stats still captures that classic "be a pro" appeal.However, any enjoyment is quickly stripped away by how incredibly lazy the rest of the package feels. The game relies on the exact same repeated animations, pre-match cutscenes, and negotiation sequences that players have seen for years. Strikingly little has changed, making the game feel almost identical not just to FC 25, but stretching all the way back to FIFA 22. Paying full price for what amounts to a squad update with recycled assets is an insulting practice, and because of this absolute lack of innovation, I cannot recommend this game.

UX/UI

User Experience is poorly designed so that you really don't know where to go, what to engage with, or what is important. Game Modes are lazily laid in different sub menus each with new tutorials and their own unique menus that don't let you navigate properly out of them, as if they are intentional independent game types while others share some data between them. As a new player to this game it is confusing to what their goal is and what you should engage with. 

As a micro transaction product, it's also confusing to know which transactions are useful.

The controls for controller are decent but overly re-use inputs that for offense and defense are counter intuitive so remapping is key. Keyboard and mouse is clearly an after thought for the design team and is a terrible experience. Menu's with keyboard and mouse are a nightmare as the mouse scrolling speed cannot be adjusted in the game and the mouse hides itself in the upper top left after a few seconds so you are constantly pulling it back. Playing with a mouse and keyboard in anything other than fullscreen with more than one monitor will pull your mouse to the outside of the screen and cause you to screw up your passing. It's confusing why this part of the product isn't seeing more attention to navigate players to a smooth clear experience. 

Gameplay 

The gameplay struggles with it's own AI, fighting you a times and helping you too much at other times. It feels like the AI is purposely making your experience un-fun by changing it's balancing at strange times and even in game to penalize you. The goalie is a terrible position and any striker remotely decent inside the box can score. The players receiving passes stop after you select the input to pass, why aren't they keeping moving in the direction of your pass like a through pass. Through passes go right to the opponent team if you don't lead far away. It doesn't seem like player techniques work properly. Physicality is random it feels like and everything is a penalty against AI at harder levels. 

Overall it feels like an arcade version of previous editions like  17 that felt more realistic despite the animations and graphics not matching todays standards. Too much attention is going into look and not enough into the player journey and experience of this AAA product. I would call this a AAA paintjob over a AA product whose business model is seasonally grifting it's players year after year.

Penalties glitched out and had to restart (yes the ai scored 3 times on beginner "play attacking highlights). Then I go to the main menu and see that none of that counted at all, not a single game. My internet cut out for 2 seconds then immediately reconnected at some point, so I get no progress in an offline mode. Trash recycled game as always. Near impossible animations to screw me over during scripted moments, having to tackle successfully 3 times to get the ball, and having to clear the ball with 3 headers in row since my players are too braindead to kick the ball sucks as always. How is player switching still so bad, have to spam it 3 times to actually get it to switch to the player with the indicator above their head. Career mode menus are still buggy, like in sim match, all tactics are assigned to the right arrow on the dpad, so no switching tactics. The throw in behind goal for a goal kick bug is still there. I love only gaining possession when surrounded by 3 opponents who immediately steal possession back after defending for 20 match minutes. And if you're going to block both the Steam overlay and Nvidia overlay from working in game, at least let me enable an in game fps counter. I honestly regret paying $13 for this, it could have been spent on much better games for the price.

Edit: Some more stuff I noticed. I was holding A to do a shoulder challenge while facing away from my goal, my player just gets given the ball, then back heels it to my keeper who gets tackled and concedes, great game design. The goal replay camera for any cross to header that results in a goal is zoomed in 2000% and you can't even see the ball at times. The wrong commentary tracks can get triggered, a bog standard breakaway, normal goal was called a back heel into a chip over the keeper by the commentators. Whenever you "jump in" to a career mode match from the sim menu, and overlay appears that says "Right stick in - Hide overlay, A - call for pass," so you have to do a flick up with the ball everytime you jump in. And I would also just like to point out how stupid the vision stat is for singleplayer modes, if you do a RTG career, starting with bad players, none of you passes will go to the player you were pointing at. I understand that in UT, with the power curve, everyone will basically have 80+ vision after the first month, but that's not how it works in singleplayer. Using the exact same stat calculations and everything for both a static mode and a mode with an ever-increasing power curve is stupid, but that is also what I expect from EA. The first portion of a match is usually smooth, but after enough time the game progressively degrades into stuttering and slow-motion gameplay, making it difficult to finish a match normally.

This was not a one-time occurrence. I reproduced the problem repeatedly across Career Mode and training sessions. Short matches sometimes complete without issue, but my normal settings (15-minute halves) consistently expose the slowdown.

I did not immediately leave a negative review. I spent many hours attempting to resolve the issue:

Verified game files.
Updated graphics drivers.
Tested different graphics settings and resolutions.
Tested different frame rate limits and V-Sync settings.
Tried compatibility settings and launch options.
Installed the latest game update.
Logged hardware telemetry during gameplay to investigate the issue.

Despite these efforts, the underlying problem remained.

Other games on my PC perform normally, so I have not found evidence that this is a general hardware problem.

I recognize that many players report playing FC 26 without issues, so I am not claiming the game is universally broken. However, there also appear to be numerous reports from PC users experiencing similar runtime slowdowns, and I was unable to find a reliable solution despite extensive troubleshooting.

Would not recommend

The Game Decides More Than You Do

EA Sports FC 26 somehow manages to make football feel less about skill and more about surviving whatever the game decides to throw at you.

Some matches are great. Others feel like the outcome was written before the first whistle. Go a couple of goals ahead and suddenly your players can't make a five-yard pass, every tackle bounces back to your opponent, your goalkeeper forgets how to save, and every loose ball magically falls to the other team.

Then there are the moments that make you wonder why you're even holding the controller. A 99 pace winger gets caught by the slowest defender on the pitch. Simple passes go in the opposite direction. Your defenders stand still while attackers walk through your back line. It feels like you're fighting the game instead of your opponent.

And when you actually need to react, the game sometimes won't even let you. In certain matches, the Team Management screen becomes inaccessible, leaving you unable to change tactics, formations, or player instructions when the match is clearly going against you. Instead of adapting, you're forced to watch your team fall apart while the game ignores your inputs.

The online experience only makes everything worse. Input delay, inconsistent responsiveness, random gameplay swings, and servers that seem to have a mind of their own make every match feel different for all the wrong reasons.

The most disappointing part is that many of these frustrations have been brought up by the community for years. Instead of delivering a polished football simulation, it often feels like the same problems return every release with a new coat of paint.

Losing because someone is better is part of football. Losing because the game feels inconsistent, buggy, and out of your control is something else entirely.

One of the most frustrating football games I've ever played. 


For everyone else: save your money, save your sanity, and go play actual football instead.

Have you ever wanted to know what it feels like to play "FIFA" for the first time again? Or maybe you're a newcomer, coming to "FIFA" for the first time off of the hype of the 2026 World Cup. 
Well boys and girls, this ain't it...

FC26 feels even more hollow now than it did in FC24 (the previous one I played) and even more than FIFA 17 (the previous one before 24) which was when I truely gave up on all hope of EA even knowing what their fans want and prioritising stakeholders over the customers that make stakeholders money. 

Manager Career Mode in FC 26 is a complete joke compared to how the game used to feel. 
- Complex tactics are completely gone, 
- The commentary is uninspired, 
- Transfers and individual player development/management are lackluster, 
- The menu navigation is clunky, minimal and dull, 
- The cinematics are the same ones we've seen for ages, 
- Press conferences literally mean nothing and there is never any unseen event or new outcome,
- Key international teams are missing, 
- Financial control and board communication are missing,
- Individual player training is missing,
- In game movement feels floaty and not fluid like it used to feel,
- And the youth squad system feels terrible. Like wtf is rush? 
We want a fully fleshed out youth squad not some bs minigame. 

I could go on forever...
And don't get me started on Ultimate Team or really any of the other game modes. 
FC in its current state the series feels discarded and shelved but you morons keep buying it every year because of UT and the cheap pachinko nature that it brings to the game, so why would they change anything? EA should be truely embarassed with where they've steered the franchise to, there has literally been not a single positive improvement I can say about manager mode in 2026 that doesn't come with far more negatives than positives. Sure it looks great but I'd take complex management depth and control over graphics any day of the week. 

The game needs a new engine and some fu*king innovation or I can see the franchise dying before the end of the decade. Sales are plummeting and people are buying the game for dirt cheap (Recently purchased for $8 AUD from the Steam Store, because I knew it would be bad). There once was a time where every year I'd be happy to shell out $70-100 for a new FIFA just to play the manager mode but that time has truely passed and gone. 

DO NOT BUY FC AT FULL PRICE UNTIL THEY INNOVATE AND LISTEN. 
STOP GAMBLING AND PLAY FIFA HOW ITS MEANT TO BE PLAYED.

Truely EA, I hope you get smoked by GTA 6 this year and you sell <5 million copies because you deserve it for handling the series so poorly. FIFA / FC could have had a complete monopoly on the soccer simulation market catering to casuals and simulation enthusiests alike but instead chose short term profit over the skill of your own game development team and the requests of tens of millions of screaming fans. 

I truely believe that if you went back to the old model of not prioritising the live service portion of your game and really kicked it out of the park with complex management modes, new game modes, the return of old spin-offs like Street and World Cup (which could be DLC) you would sell a boatload.

Aside from Ran/Actua Soccer back in '94/'95, the first soccer game I played extensively was PES 2009. I compared them again today, and not much has changed since then. Sure, the graphics are a bit better, and everything is a little more polished.
But we’re talking about 16 years of development. Especially when comparing it to its immediate predecessors, the question arises: What is actually being improved here? What justifies buying a new full-priced copy every year? It’s almost an insult that EA releases the same game year after year and charges full price for it. FC 26 is actually really enjoyable, especially for me because this is my first FC game. I had a great time playing it and overall the experience was much better than I expected.

The biggest problem is the optimization. The game runs badly on higher settings, and the FPS can start dropping even before the match begins. I had to play on low graphics for almost my entire playtime. I would recommend watching a few YouTube videos or checking Reddit for the best settings to reduce FPS drops. After changing the settings properly, the game feels much smoother.

One of the main reasons I liked the game is because I got it for only ₹150, which is around $1.57. For that price, it was completely worth it. It still has a lot of bugs, glitches and performance issues, but at such a low price, I can ignore most of them.

I would not recommend buying it at full price because it is definitely not worth that much in its current condition. But if you get it again for ₹150 or even lower, then it is a good deal.

For people who have never played any FIFA or FC game before, I would definitely recommend trying it during a sale. You may enjoy it more than people who keep comparing it with older FC games.

There is a particular kind of disappointment that comes with buying a new sports game. You know going in that it’s going to be flawed. You expect the reused animations, the ignored bugs, and the bare-bones updates. But somehow, EA Sports FC 26 manages to dip below even the rock-bottom expectations set by FC 25. Let’s be clear: FC 25 was a mess. But FC 26 is FC 25 after a lobotomy. EA has somehow achieved negative progress, taking a game that was already worse than its predecessor and stripping out whatever remaining joy was left. 

If you thought the gameplay in FC 25 was sluggish and unresponsive, congratulations, EA heard your complaints and made it worse. The much-hyped "new physics engine" feels like you’re playing football in a swimming pool filled with wet concrete. Input delay is the real star of the show this year; you can press the pass button, go make a cup of coffee, come back, and maybe, just maybe your player will actually pass the ball.

Defensive AI is completely non-existent. Your backline will part like the Red Sea the second an opponent triggers a run, seemingly baffled by the concept of marking. Meanwhile, your attackers will stand motionless, offside, refusing to make a darting run unless you manually pilot them with a thumbstick while fighting the clunky player-switching mechanics. 

And the scripting? It’s worse than ever. We all know "EA FC Magic" exists, but in FC 26, it feels less like subtle momentum shifting and more like the game actively wrestling the controller out of your hands. Your 99-rated striker will miss an open net, your goalkeeper will intentionally parry the ball directly into the path of the only opposing attacker in the box, and you are left staring at the screen wondering why you spent $70 to be gaslit by an algorithm.

Ultimate Team
Remember when Ultimate Team was actually fun to play without spending real money? Those days are long gone. FC 26’s economy is a blatant, shameless cash grab. The grind is longer, the pack weights are abysmal, and the power curve is designed to make you feel inadequate unless you buy FIFA—sorry, *FC*—Points. 

EA has packed the UI with so many modes, evolutions, and SBCs that navigating the menu feels like doing your taxes. It’s a casino disguised as a football game, and the house always wins. The worst part? The servers still run on what feels like a 2008 dial-up connection. You’ll spend half your weekend league watching the latency ping bounce between 15ms and 150ms while your players teleport across the pitch. 

Career Mode
Career mode continues to be the neglected middle child. EA added a few new cinematic cutscenes for press conferences, but underneath that thin veneer of paint, it’s the exact same mode we’ve had for five years. The same bugs from FC 25? Still here. Youth academy players still develop weirdly, transfer logic still makes zero sense, and the AI managers still behave like they’ve never watched a football match in their lives. 

Graphics and Presentation
Visually, FC 26 is indistinguishable from FC 25, which was indistinguishable from FIFA 23. The crowds still look like cardboard cutouts, the stadiums still have lighting glitches, and the commentary team still cycles through the same five phrases, often reacting to a goal that happened three plays ago. 

EA Sports FC 26 isn’t a video game; it’s an annual update to a live-service slot machine. It is worse than FC 25, which was worse than FIFA 23. It is a staggering achievement in regression. EA knows they have a monopoly on licensed football, and FC 26 is the ultimate proof that they simply do not care. 

If you bought FC 25, you got ripped off. If you buy FC 26, you are paying full price to be abused again. Do yourself a favor: save your money, go outside, play a game of real football, or just keep playing whatever version of the game you currently own. There is nothing to see here.

I highly recommend FC 26 to anyone who enjoys soccer, sports games, or even just fun multiplayer games. In my opinion, it is one of the most complete football games available because there is always something to do, whether you enjoy competitive matches, building your dream team, or simply playing with friends.

One of the biggest reasons I recommend FC 26 is the gameplay. The matches feel exciting because every game is different. You have to think about your tactics, passing, defending, dribbling, and shooting instead of just pressing random buttons. Winning a close match feels rewarding because your decisions and skill make a real difference. Whether you're playing against the AI or real people online, every match keeps you engaged and wanting to improve.

Another great feature is Ultimate Team. Building your own squad is one of the most enjoyable parts of the game. You can earn coins, complete challenges, open packs, trade on the market, and slowly improve your team over time. There are thousands of players from leagues all around the world, so you can create almost any squad you can imagine. You can build a team with your favorite club, your country's national players, or even create a squad full of football legends.

The amount of content in FC 26 is another reason why it's worth recommending. There are daily objectives, weekly rewards, Squad Building Challenges, special events, promotions, live content, and seasonal rewards that constantly give you something new to work toward. Even if you only play for a short amount of time each day, you'll usually have new goals to complete and rewards to earn.

Career Mode is another fantastic part of the game. If you've ever dreamed of managing your favorite club, signing superstar players, developing young talent, scouting future stars, or leading a small club to win major trophies, Career Mode lets you do all of that. You can also create your own player and experience the journey from a young prospect to becoming one of the best footballers in the world.

For players who enjoy online competition, FC 26 has many different modes that challenge you against other people. Climbing divisions, improving your rank, and testing your skills against players from around the world creates exciting moments that never get old. Every victory feels earned, and every loss teaches you something that can help you become a better player.

One thing I really appreciate is the variety. If you get tired of one mode, you can switch to another. You can play Ultimate Team, Clubs, Kick-Off, Career Mode, tournaments, skill games, or friendly matches with family and friends. Because there are so many options, the game rarely becomes boring.

The graphics are another reason I recommend FC 26. The stadiums look realistic, the crowds create an exciting atmosphere, and many player faces and animations are detailed enough to make matches feel like watching a real football broadcast. The lighting, weather effects, celebrations, and presentation all help make every game feel more immersive.

Customization is another strong point. You can personalize your club with unique kits, stadium themes, badges, tifos, goal songs, celebrations, chants, and cosmetic items. This allows every player to make their club feel unique and represent their own style.

FC 26 also helps players learn more about football. As you play, you naturally begin to understand formations, tactics, pressing, possession, counterattacks, player roles, chemistry, and how different playstyles affect the game. Even people who are newer to soccer can develop a better understanding of how the sport works.

The game is also fun with friends. Whether you're playing online, sitting together on the couch, or competing against each other, FC 26 creates memorable moments. Close matches, last-minute goals, incredible saves, and amazing celebrations often become stories you'll remember long after the game ends.

One of the best things about FC 26 is that there is always room to improve. Even experienced players continue learning new skills, dribbling techniques, passing combinations, defensive strategies, and shooting methods. Every match becomes an opportunity to become a better player, making progress feel satisfying.

The soundtrack and overall presentation also deserve recognition. The music, menus, commentary, and stadium atmosphere help make the game enjoyable even when you're not actually playing a match. Everything feels polished and designed to keep players entertained.

FC 26 is also regularly updated throughout the year with new content, events, player upgrades, and special promotions. This keeps the game fresh and gives players reasons to return regularly instead of feeling like they've already completed everything.

Whether you're a casual player who only wants to play a few matches after school or work, or a competitive player who wants to reach the highest divisions, FC 26 offers something for everyone. You can enjoy it at your own pace while constantly finding new goals to work toward.

Overall, I would absolutely recommend FC 26 because it combines exciting gameplay, realistic football, excellent graphics, multiple game modes, endless customization, regular updates, rewarding progression, and countless hours of entertainment. It offers something for nearly every type of player, whether you're a lifelong football fan or someone trying the sport for the first time. Every match feels like a new challenge, every improvement feels rewarding, and every season brings new experiences. For anyone looking for a fun, competitive, and enjoyable football game with lots of replay value, FC 26 is definitely worth playing.

After 1121 hours, I honestly cannot recommend EA SPORTS FC 26.

The core problem is not that I lose matches. Losing is fine when the game feels fair and responsive. The problem is that too many important moments feel out of my control.

Player switching with the right stick is extremely inconsistent. In defensive situations, especially inside or around the box, the game often selects the wrong player or refuses to switch to the obvious defender. This makes manual defending feel random instead of skill-based.

The defensive AI is also very poor. Center backs often leave strikers completely open in the box, while the same simple attacking patterns work again and again. A player can run down the wing almost to the goal line, cut the ball back into the box, and somehow the defenders keep making the same mistakes. It feels less like football and more like abusing a broken script.

Online responsiveness is another major issue. In a competitive game, connection quality should matter much more. I should be able to choose to play only against opponents with very low latency, for example under 16 ms. Instead, many matches feel delayed, heavy and inconsistent, which completely changes the gameplay.

The game has good presentation, lots of content, and the usual addictive football loop. But after so many hours, the frustrating parts are impossible to ignore. EA needs to seriously fix player switching, defensive AI, online responsiveness, latency filtering and repetitive exploit mechanics.

Until then, I cannot recommend this game.

❌ The UI Still Sucks: The menus are sluggish and a confusing maze more than ever.

❌ Older FIFAs Were Just Better: The franchise lost its soul. The classic games actually had physical ball weight, organic momentum, balanced gameplay, and better physics.


The Good:
✅ Career Mode is Still Half-Decent: If you stay far away from the online sweat lords, Career Mode is the only saving grace. It’s actually a fun place to build a squad and enjoy a proper football fix.

✅ "Authentic Mode" is a Lifesaver: Flipping the offline preset to Authentic Mode fixes some of the crazy pace, adding real physical weight back to the ball. This Authentic Mode setting should be the default for online play too.


The Verdict
Stop wasting your cash on Ultimate Team packs and stop feeding the hype by subscribing to UT content creators. Ultimate Team has completely ruined this franchise, and supporting it just keeps making the game worse every single year.

Congratulations, EA. Every year I wonder how it's possible to lower the bar, and every year you somehow treat it as a challenge instead of a warning. I bought a football game expecting to play football. Instead, I found myself participating in what feels like an unpaid quality assurance program. After more than 1.5 hours, I still hadn't actually played. That's honestly impressive in a way I never wanted to experience.
The controller randomly disconnects for no apparent reason, as if it has a better understanding of what's happening than I do and simply decides to leave. Ultimate Team, one of the main reasons many people buy the game, refuses to open. At this point it feels less like a game mode and more like a mythical creature—everyone talks about it, but actually seeing it is another story.
The menus deserve a special award. Every click is followed by another loading screen, giving you enough time to reconsider your purchase, browse the internet, make coffee, or wonder how software in 2026 can feel slower than games released over a decade ago. And somehow there's still no simple "Accept All" button. Instead, you're expected to go through endless prompts one by one, waiting after every confirmation like you're completing paperwork rather than launching a video game.
It's fascinating how so much effort seems to have gone into selling Ultimate Team packs, while basic usability appears to have been treated as an optional feature. The priorities are impossible to miss. Everything surrounding the store works remarkably well, while the actual game struggles to reach the starting line.
What makes this even more disappointing is that none of these problems feel surprising anymore. Every release seems to follow the same pattern: launch first, let customers discover the issues, and fix them later—if they get fixed at all. At some point this stops looking like bad luck and starts looking like the business model.
I wasn't expecting perfection. Bugs happen. But I was expecting a product that lets me play football without spending hours troubleshooting, restarting, reconnecting controllers, waiting through endless loading screens, and hoping that the next menu might finally work.
Right now, this doesn't feel like a finished game. It feels like early access with a full-price tag. The most realistic part of EA Sports FC 26 isn't the football—it's the feeling of paying premium money for promises that might eventually become reality. Until then, the hardest match in the game isn't against another player. It's against the menu.

I wouldn't recommend this game for several reasons.
First of all, the game is full of bugs. I'm mainly referring to menu bugs, loading issues when entering the game, and problems when switching between different menus. The Premium Shop is especially frustrating. Sometimes the game completely freezes when you enter it, and you can only navigate inside the shop itself. The only way to get out is to close the game entirely. Another major issue is the audio. Everything works except the commentators, who are often completely silent, making matches feel lifeless.

Ultimate Team has become even more pay-to-win than before. While the gameplay is slightly better than in FC 25, there are still many problems. Long shots have been heavily nerfed, and finesse shots are much less effective than they used to be. On the positive side, goalkeepers are noticeably better and make more realistic saves.One thing that really bothers me is the physical contact between players. Defending doesn't feel natural at all. When two players collide or fight for possession, there is almost no sense of physical interaction. Compared to eFootball, the difference is huge. Although sliding tackles can still be effective, the overall physicality feels weak and unrealistic.

The servers are another disappointment. Rivals is relatively stable most of the time, but Champions and several other online modes often suffer from poor server performance, resulting in lag and inconsistent gameplay.

There are also many missing licenses. The FIFA Club World Cup mode, which is currently taking place, feels rushed and unfinished. There are no meaningful live updates based on players' real-life performances outside of Ultimate Team. The lack of official licensing for the tournament also takes away much of the atmosphere.

Another disappointing omission is the inability to play the Club World Cup online with a friend while enjoying the full tournament atmosphere. Yes, you can still select most of the national teams and clubs in regular exhibition modes, but it's simply not the same experience.

Overall, I would only recommend buying this game if you can find it for around €20 or less. Anything above that is simply not worth the money. There are some improvements compared to last year's game, but the number of bugs, missing features, server issues, and gameplay flaws make it very difficult to recommend at full price.

Every year, I tell myself: this is the year EA finally does it. This is the year they cook. And every year, EA hands me a lukewarm meal, charges me €70 for it, and somehow convinces half the internet it's Michelin-starred.

EA Sports FC 26 is, in the most generous possible terms, a game that exists. It boots up. The ball is round. The goals are still rectangular. Well done, everyone. Take the rest of the year off.

The big headline feature this year is two gameplay modes: Competitive and Authentic. Competitive is the arcade chaos you already know and tolerate. Authentic is slower, more realistic, and slightly more painful — much like the experience of buying this game in the first place. My AI defenders have clearly chosen the Authentic experience of standing completely still while the opposition waltzes past them into the net.

Visually? Stunning. Genuinely beautiful. The players look so lifelike that you can almost see the disappointment in their eyes when they, too, realize they're in FC 26.

Ultimate Team is, as always, the crown jewel — if the crown were made of microtransactions and the jewels were player packs you'd need a second mortgage to open. EA has infused this beloved series with microtransactions that many describe as shameful, alongside a truly underwhelming season pass. But hey, for just €4.99 you can get a player who runs slightly faster. Progress! 

And yes, overall user reviews on Steam sit at "Mixed". That means the majority of people who paid full price are out there, right now, also not enjoying themselves. There's a real community feel to that. 

In summary: FC 26 is the gaming equivalent of paying rent — you do it every year, you don't love it, and you're not entirely sure what you're getting in return. But what choice do you have? There's no other football game. EA knows this. EA has always known this.

Buy it? No. Will I buy it next year? ...Probably.

Fun Gameplay Saved by the Modding Community
Playing EA Sports FC 26 on PC offers a very solid and enjoyable core gameplay experience. On the pitch, the mechanics feel just right and provide a satisfying virtual football experience. However, beneath that fun, there are some major caveats that make the "vanilla" experience (base game without mods) feel underwhelming and quickly get boring.

Here is the breakdown of my experience with EA Sports FC 26:

The Pros
Solid Core Gameplay: The feel of the game, player controls, and match flow are genuinely fun. The fundamental gameplay is still the main draw that keeps you hooked on the pitch.

The Cons & Critical Notes
Boring Base Game: When played purely vanilla without any community mods, the game loses its charm fast. The default atmosphere and details from EA just aren't strong enough to keep you engaged in the long run.

Outshined by Modders' Creativity: The modding community (using mods like FIFER, etc.) proves capable of providing much richer and more interesting variety. From more accurate player faces and diverse kits to the presence of club mascots that bring the stadium to life. The visual limitations in the base game mean PC players inevitably have to rely on mods to get the optimal visual experience.

Stagnant Career Mode (Copy-Paste from FC 25): This is the biggest letdown, especially since I already played EA FC 25 (on my other Steam account). There are zero innovations, new features, or meaningful overhauls in the FC 26 Career Mode. The transition feels exactly like playing last year's game.

Conclusion
EA Sports FC 26 is fundamentally a mechanically fun game. However, its full potential and visual appeal only truly "come alive" when injected with third-party mods. If you are a PC player who purely relies on EA's default modes, and a Career Mode lover expecting a significant upgrade from FC 25, this year's release will feel like a full-priced roster update. I can only recommend this game if you are willing to put in the time to install mods to enrich your overall experience.

A Note for the Future:
I sincerely hope that EA Sports FC 27 will bring real improvements across the board, particularly for Career Mode (both Manager and Player). EA needs to make the Career Mode much more engaging, dynamic, and innovative so it stops feeling like the exact same game as the previous entries. We need real changes, not just the same mode recycled year after year.

After spending time with EA SPORTS FC 26, I can say that I have enjoyed the game overall. The gameplay is fun, matches are exciting, and there is plenty of content to keep football fans entertained.

There are a few areas that could be improved. In my experience, passing felt slightly better and more consistent in FC 25. If passing responsiveness was improved in future updates, the gameplay would feel even better.

Another point is the World Cup content. While FC 26 does not have the official FIFA World Cup 2026 license, I still enjoyed playing the World Cup-style tournament mode. It may not have the official FIFA branding, but it is still fun and captures much of the excitement of an international tournament.

One thing I did not like was the lack of some player face scans. While playing with Brazil, I noticed that several players did not have their proper faces, including Neymar. This was a little disappointing and reduced the overall authenticity of the team. I have not checked every national team, but it was noticeable with Brazil.

The biggest positive for me is the value for money. I purchased FC 26 during a sale for only ₹150, which is an excellent price for the amount of content included. At that price, I feel I received great value and many hours of entertainment.

EA Sports also continues to release a new football game almost every year, and after a few months these games are often heavily discounted, making them affordable for many players. That is something I personally appreciate.

FC 26 is not perfect, but it is still a fun football game that I can recommend, especially when purchased during a sale.

Verdict: Recommended.

The game starts off reasonably well, running at around 60 FPS, but after the first half, the frame rate drops dramatically to as low as 5 FPS. Once this happens, the game becomes practically unplayable, with severe stuttering and input lag.

If you're using a 4GB graphics card like the GTX 1650, I would strongly advise against buying or playing this title until the developers address the optimization issues. The VRAM usage appears to be poorly managed, causing performance to degrade over time rather than remain consistent throughout a match.

For players with similar hardware, you're honestly better off sticking with other older FIFA titles, which provide a much smoother and more enjoyable experience on mid-range systems.

Pros:

Decent visuals and performance at the start.
Gameplay feels fine when FPS is stable.

Cons:

Massive FPS drops during longer play sessions.
Performance falls from 60 FPS to around 5 FPS.
Unplayable on 4GB GPUs like the GTX 1650.
Poor optimization and possible VRAM management issues.

Verdict: 2/10 – Not recommended for GTX 1650 4GB users. Until optimization improves, older FIFA titles offer a far better experience on this hardware.

The Verdict: EA Sports has officially turned a historic football franchise into an unplayable, profit-first physics experiment. If you love football and want a game where your actual skill determines the outcome, look elsewhere.
​1. The Death of Skill Gap: Sluggish One Game, Superpowers the Next
​The most frustrating thing about FC 26 is the utter lack of consistency. In one match, your players move smoothly, execute commands instantly, and feel like world-class professionals. In the very next match, they feel like they are running through thick mud, turning like cargo ships, and ignoring your basic controller inputs.
​EA continues to force aggressive, broken AI assistance and "dynamic difficulty" down our throats. Instead of letting us use our own skill, the game heavily relies on scripted momentum shifts. You aren't playing against your opponent; you are playing against the game's AI determining who "deserves" to win.  
​2. "Useless AI Assistance" Ruining the Defending and Passing
​EA advertised major tactical overhauls, but the reality is a complete mess. Manual defending has been essentially killed off. The game actively punishes you for trying to time tackles manually, while letting "rats" run around with a single midfielder while the AI auto-defends perfectly for them.
​Passing is completely randomized by RNG (random number generation). Simple five-yard passes go wildly off-target, while overpowered, unrealistic through-balls slice through defenses without any logic. It strips away any sense of football knowledge or strategic buildup.  
​3. All About Profit, Zero Care for the Community
​It is blatantly obvious that the developers at EA are lazy and detached from what the community actually wants. Year after year, the same core bugs, server lag, and input delays are completely ignored.
​Instead of fixing the core gameplay mechanics, EA directs 100% of their energy into pushing microtransactions, store packs, and FOMO (fear of missing out) content. The game feels less like a competitive sports simulator and more like a casino built around football skin mechanics.
​Final Thoughts
​We just want to play normal football. We want a game where input delay doesn't exist, where player stats remain consistent from match to match, and where the better player actually wins. FC 26 is a massive disappointment that thrives on player frustration. Save your money and your sanity.

I wanted to enjoy FC 26, but the performance issues completely ruin the experience.

The game runs fine at first, but after playing for a while usually around halftime the FPS suddenly drops and stays low. It feels like there's some kind of broken FPS limiter or performance bug kicking in during matches. Restarting the game temporarily fixes it, but then the problem comes back again.

What's frustrating is that my hardware isn't the issue. Many players are reporting similar problems, yet these performance issues still exist. A football game shouldn't require troubleshooting every match just to maintain stable framerates.

Gameplay can be enjoyable when the game actually runs properly, but technical problems like this make it hard to recommend. For a full-priced AAA sports title, I expected much better optimization and quality control.

Until EA addresses the FPS drops and performance instability, I can't recommend FC 26.

Pros:

Fun gameplay when performance is stable
Updated teams and content

Cons:

Severe FPS drops after extended play
Possible broken FPS limiter/performance bug
Requires restarting the game to restore performance
Poor optimization for a AAA release

Disappointing release. Technical issues overshadow the football. ⚽💔

Meta Gaming in these kind of game modes ruins everything. So i played it for not even a month, got a 93 rated & 33 chem team and realized all the problems people are complaining about are exactly true.

I've been playing FIFA/EA FC for well over a decade, and at this point I honestly think EA FC 26 is less of a football game and more of a psychological experiment designed to test how much frustration a human being can tolerate before uninstalling.

Every year EA talks about realism, but somehow my players still manage to forget they're professional footballers halfway through a match. One game my striker moves like prime Messi, the next game he turns like a refrigerator that's been dragged across a parking lot.

The passing is comedy gold. I'll aim a simple pass to the player standing right in front of me, and EA FC 26 decides that what I actually meant was a 40-yard through ball directly to the opponent. Thanks EA, glad the game knows what I want better than I do.

Defending is even funnier. You make the perfect tackle, win the ball cleanly, and somehow it ricochets back to the attacker. Then again. Then again. At this point I don't think I'm defending against another player, I'm defending against the laws of physics coded by EA.

And don't get me started on player switching. Nothing beats watching a dangerous counterattack and switching between three completely irrelevant players while the guy you actually want to control is just standing there admiring the grass.

The most impressive feature in EA FC 26 isn't HyperMotion, tactical AI, or whatever marketing buzzword they're using this year. It's EA's ability to convince me that maybe THIS tackle, THIS interception, or THIS rebound will finally work as intended. It never does, but somehow I keep believing.

At this point I don't need new animations or new card designs. I just want my players to behave like they remember they're getting paid millions a week and not like eleven random dudes who met in the parking lot five minutes before kickoff.

See you all tomorrow when I inevitably launch the game again.

For players with similar hardware, you're honestly better off sticking with FIFA 19 or other older FIFA titles, which provide a much smoother and more enjoyable experience on mid-range systems.

Pros:

Gameplay feels fine when FPS is stable.

Cons:

Verdict: 2/10 – Not recommended for GTX 1650 4GB users. Until optimization improves, FIFA 19 offers a far better experience on this hardware.

As with any yearly title (not just EA), wait for a sale. They might deserve your money every 3 or 4 years, but not every year. If every year they gave people who have last year's version a 50% discount, I might consider buying every year. No yearly title adds enough in the following year to merit another 60+ bucks. I bought it for 20 bucks and for that price it's a steal. I'd pay 40 tops.

I'd love nothing more than to say 'Not Recommended, go buy this other really good footy game', but sadly such a game does not yet exist (outside of mod projects for PES 21). It's also true that this is a decent game. So I will recommend it with the caveat that it most likely is NOT worth buying at full price if you own FC25. I do not, so pinch of salt there.

That said, there are some issues... 

I have to open Task Manager and end all EA processes each time I start the game up. The game tries to open, and doesn't. Each time I try to open the game it adds another EA process. When I use taskman, it solves the problem though.

The Menus are weird. So much so that if you aren't paying attention you can accidentally end up playing a monetised game mode from almost any menu in any mode. 

Player Career camera breaks at half time if you hold to skip and you can't see what's going on in the match for the second half. You basically have to skip to result

Gameplay is slightly improved on FIFA 23. I haven't noticed any of that circumstantial scripting that everyone who plays knows exists but EA still deny... So that's a plus.

They must have lost some licenses because there are a lot of matchday sound effects and chants, etc, that were in previous versions but are not in this one.

One of the (English language) commentators sounds like an AI. Fortunately you can manually remove only him in the options.

There are various choices in career mode that you have to mess around with the left stick trying to get them to be highlighted so you can choose them. Hard to explain this, but the diagonals on the left stick are very finicky.

We still have far too many impossible shots on the higher difficulties. That they exist is fine, and that there are more of them is also fine, but it seems like any forward is able to curl into the top corner with his back to goal and through a defender. It's a minor gripe, but it is a thing nonetheless.

TL/DR: It scratches the same itch EA's footy game has always scratched and I am enjoying the game the same way I did previous versions. Game is okay, but very buggy. I wish I had an "Informal" option for this one.

I have quite a lot of visual (flickering, missing textures, etc) and gameplay bugs. Like how players sometimes don't behave the way they should. But not the "EA decided I lose, so I lose" way, but the "I'm convinced this is genuinely a bug" way.

Besides the bugs, the gameplay is okay. I've played worse FIFA games before, but PES is still miles better. For example, the players in this game are way too quick to react to input, which is great for an arcade game, but not so much for a simulation, which this game also claims to be. PES somehow hit the sweetspot between movability and a certain heft to the players. Also, there is barely any movement in your team, when you try to get the ball to the front. I regularly find myself just kicking the ball around in the back, hoping to find an opening, but none of my players try to offer themselves as that player that makes a move happen. Again, something PES did way better, especially considering, I'm actually telling my players to play counter attack, yet none of my players seem interested in playing counter attack, something that actually doesn't happen in PES. Speaking of things that don't happen in PES, due to the problem of no player trying to make a move, I often also lose the ball when passing it around in the back, because all of my players are right next to an opponent. Also something that doesn't happen in PES, where players are trying to move away from opponents in an attempt to get the ball.

Some other gripes of mine are the gameplay being too fast, even when set to "Realism" (again something that PES did really well and something FIFA/EA FC just hasn't been able to replicate, but it actually got way worse compared to EA FC 24), passes feeling extremely mechanical (PES actually had a really great way of handling that, which took some time getting used to, but was fantastic and way more realistic than what EA FC 26 offers) and goalkeepers being as terrible as they've been 10 years ago, when they got their last upgrade (also something PES actually doesn't suffer from, since goalkeepers feel actually realistic there).

In the end, this game will certainly entertain me for quite a few hours, but I will return to playing PES 2020 again eventually, since so far, no other football game has been able to rival the fluidity and natural feeling of it's gameplay. Besides eFootball since about a year after it's release, but I'm a career mode player and KONAMI decided to strip the game of a career mode entirely, so I'm stuck with PES 2020 or EA FC...
