FC 26 – 3/10 – Fun Game, But Unplayable on Steam Due to Constant Crashes

FC 26 had all the makings of a solid, fun football game. The gameplay is engaging, with fluid mechanics and a satisfying level of control over your team. The matches are intense, the player movements are smooth, and the action feels just right when it works. For a moment, it seems like the perfect pick for casual football fans or those looking for a quick but enjoyable gaming experience. Unfortunately, that's where the praise ends—because the game simply doesn’t work properly on Steam.

The major issue with FC 26 is its stability. Despite the fun gameplay on offer, the game crashes frequently, making it nearly impossible to get through a full match or enjoy any extended sessions. Whether it's a random freeze mid-game, crashing to the desktop after loading a match, or losing progress after an unexpected shutdown, the game’s technical issues ruin what could have been an otherwise enjoyable experience. At this point, FC 26 feels like it’s been released in an unfinished state on Steam, with no clear fixes in sight.

When it does work, the game is fun. The mechanics are solid, the visuals are decent (if not groundbreaking), and the sound design—while nothing special—provides a good atmosphere during matches. There’s a satisfying sense of progression, team management, and strategy that could keep you invested for hours. If the game ran smoothly, it’d be a decent football sim. However, these positives are completely overshadowed by the constant crashes that prevent any meaningful progress.

The fact that FC 26 is unplayable on Steam is a huge issue, and it’s disappointing because the game has potential. For players who are able to get through a match without it crashing, there’s a solid experience waiting for them, but that’s a big “if.” The lack of a reliable experience on such a major platform makes it hard to recommend.

If you’re still determined to play it, I highly suggest buying it through the EA App instead. It seems to be more stable there, and you’ll actually be able to enjoy the game without the constant crashing and frustration that comes with the Steam version.

FC 26 3/10 – A Fun Game, If You Can Actually Play It
FC 26 could have been a solid sports title, but the constant crashing makes it unplayable for most players on Steam. The potential is there, but it’s buried under a mountain of technical issues. Until the developers address the stability problems, this game is more frustrating than fun. If you're looking for a working football game, you’re better off buying it on the EA App, where the experience is at least more reliable.

I grew up dreaming of owning a FIFA game. Back then, money was tight, and the idea of finally playing it felt like a milestone. Fast forward to today, I finally own it—and the experience has been nothing short of disappointing.
Performance Issues
- FPS drops: The game frequently dips to single-digit frames, making matches feel unplayable.
- Controller delay: Inputs lag, leaving me frustrated as players fail to respond in crucial moments.
- Gameplay stutters: Sometimes, players just stop moving mid-game, breaking immersion completely.
Server & Optimization
It’s not just me—many players online report the same problems. EA’s servers feel unreliable, and the game itself is poorly optimized. For a title that costs so much, this level of instability is unacceptable.
Final Verdict
Owning FIFA was once a dream. Playing it has turned into a nightmare. Between the broken servers, unresponsive gameplay, and lack of optimization, this is the last FIFA/EA FC title I’ll ever buy. It’s simply not worth the money—or the sanity it drains.

The number of random disconnects, server timeouts, and random bugs I encounter in this game would make me believe this was an early access beta. The animations are poor, as evidenced by watching some goal instant replays and seeing collision physics poorly integrated with balls going through people's legs and body parts morphing together. It's a true shame how inconsistent it really is. 
Furthermore, having played mostly Player Career mode in every FIFA game I played, I can say this is an extremely disappointing showing from EA FC 26. Going back to FIFA 17 and seeing how much effort they put into The Journey, allowing you to truly immerse yourself into a story was fantastic. It's saddening to see their pure focus on Ultimate Team and the lack of effort that results in other gameplay modes. 
Finally, it's just too easy to progress both in UT and Career Mode. In previous games, you would start UT with a bronze squad and celebrate when you finally could afford your first gold player. An 80 rated squad was something that took genuine effort, where now you are gifted 90 OVR players from the moment you start the game. In Player Career, you used to start out as a 65 OVR and be sent on loan to third division teams to prove your worth. You would have to genuinely grind and immerse yourself in the game to succeed, and now none of that exists. 
Overall, its fun to play as an arcade game, but as the number one Football video game on the market, it is extremely flawed.

FC 26 is a bold experiment in redefining what football means. 

Passing is optional and completely broken. You press pass, something happens, and you’re left to interpret the result like modern art. Was that a through ball? A clearance? A quiet cry for help from the physics engine? Hard to say, but it’s rarely accurate, and never what you intended. 

Your players actively avoid useful positions. There’s something almost artistic about watching them hide behind defenders or sprint into the same five square meters like it’s a team-building exercise. To be fair, this does add a certain difficulty curve. Just not the fun kind. On a casual level, it’s less "pick up and play" and more “pick up and question your life choices.” You’re not battling the opponent so much as negotiating with your own team, hoping that at least two of them will behave like professional footballers for a few seconds in a row. 

Overall, FC 26 is perfect if you enjoy unpredictability, chaos, and shouting “why are you THERE?” at your screen. If you’re looking for responsive passing, intelligent positioning, or anything resembling tactical awareness, consider it an opportunity to practice patience instead. Lots and lots of patience.

This game is Not for Ryzen 6000 series processors, I've been trying to play this game for 17hrs and still i couldn't play it tried to fix it but nothing happen. This game is unable to create a shader file in Documents and due to this its locking my FPS to 7 as Ryzen 6000 series processors runs on 2 types of cores i.e. P-core(performance core) , E-core( Efficiency core).

When I researched about it I've come to a realisation that its anti cheat is interfering with the processors by watching CPU threads movement across P/E cores(performance /Efficiency cores) and activates a fail safe that makes the game not save the shaders and drop and lock to 7 FPS

So basically, the root cause is the CPU scheduler conflict on Ryzen 7 6800H Laptops
-> fc 26 + anti cheat detects thread movement between P-cores and E-cores
->Anti-Cheat enters failsafe mode, locking FPS to ~7, even though GPU is fully used
-> windows tweaks , shader cache, or reinstall cannot fix the underlying scheduler conflict

This year's career mode is genuinly painful to play. I'm the type of a player that always plays sim only, so maybe I'm missing out on the "amazing" on pitch gameplay but my god, the simulation is so broken now. 

- The quick sim option is still broken, as it is every year, with it basically being a glorified random number generator. 
- Simulation option is the definition of nothing ever happens. Games usually end 0-0 or at most 1-0, partly because the "half length" option apparently doesn't influence the sim length, with the halves being always like 1 to 2 mins long, which is too short for the AI to do anything.
- The tactical view sim was a promising idea, but it was kind of botched. The "manager view" camera is broken, with your manager character blocking 30% of your FOV 75% of the time. Fortunately, you can switch to the classic TV camera, which is a small plus for EA. But on a second thought, maybe not seeing the game would have been better for my sanity. I had AI on legendary and it was still dumb as ****. No crosses, barely any runs, no riskier long balls or shots from distance. The players either pass the ball back and forth between 2 or 3 guys or play handball tactics with passing around the penalty box waiting for any opening. And when the opening shows, they usually just pass back or try to dribble in the pen box and inevitably lose the ball. Watching AI vs Ai game is genuine suffering at this point. And still, games usually end with 0 or 1 goal from both teams combined, 2 if you are lucky.

And sure, there are some fun new features like the much needed assistant coaches that work well, the overhauled training plans which I think are decent, the on and off the ball playstyles and roles, which are a step in the right direction but have flaws. Like why cant I play a different formation on and off the ball? Doesn't it kind of kill the purpose of having two separate views for it? But what's the point of all those "cherries" if the "cake", so the actual matches are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful? I get that FUT is the main cash cow for EA, but at this point it feels like CM is an afterthought, with it being worked on maybe for two weeks before EA allocates the manpower to FUT.

I am appalled by this game honestly, I only spent £16 to get it, and it would be bad even for a free game.

Plus points: There are quite a few real player faces, the graphics in general are not bad, and the idea of the manager market is good. 

Overall, this game is underwhelming, I am a career mode player, and it could not be clearer how little EA care about the career mode player base. 

Transfer logic is terrible, it could be worse, but not by much: 
Madrid consistently buy 4-5 world class centre backs, Arsenal will end up with 3 top left backs and 2 world class aging keepers, Bilbao don't have a basque policy, relegated teams keep top players, promoted teams don't sign players at the level to be in the next league.... I could go on, but bottom line - LAZY programming, not enough thought put in. 

Player personality, contract situation, manager personality/style, all severely lacking or non existent.
This leads to a stale career mode that at best is half decent for a season maybe 2 at a stretch, which is sad, because I used to love having one or two deep saves that carried through 10+ seasons.

Gameplay is just about okay, but only really passable with way too much tweaking to sliders, modding, or both, all of which has to be reviewed every patch release. I have personally played FIFA since 2000 and the gameplay for a long time has been frustrating. It is either way too punishing and stale, far too end to end, or way too easy, with basically no middle ground. 

Playstyles, tactics, and formations are just bad and/or pointless, there was a time around FIFA 16ish when I feel it was good, with players gaining traits as they got better based on attirbutes (85 vision/86 short pass = Playmaker trait for example). Formations and tactics are rigid, uniform, and kill creativity, making everything an either/or decision on how the player wants to play. When we could move players around and create formations it was overall a much better experience. Also the whole process is horribly clunky and slow - I may have 2 in game minutes left and want to bring on a centre back for a CAM, and I spend 2 or 3 times the amount of time making that change, than actually finishing the game. 

Kits and player faces. There is no way Leicester City have only two blue kits in real life, they use a third kit, and generally we see teams mix and match their sock/short/tops in real life... so we should be able to do it in game. I am sick of having to break the emersion by playing the home team in their away kit, or play a generally confusing game where the kits clash. 
Player faces are just sad really, Saka only just got his adult face added this year, but then Eberechi Eze is still 22 years old, Madueke looks like a child, Calafiori hasn't got a face, club captain Martin Odegaard doesn't look like him, Viktor Gyokeres has scored over 100 goals in the past 2 seasons, and still doesn't have a celebration. All more than enough reasons for me to not play with my team in career mode. 

Playing the game for a few years now has only been pallatable, bearable and semi-enjoyable with mods. But it seems that fc26 mods just haven't worked for me, my PC doesn't like them, and I haven't been able to fix it. 

99% of my enjoyment has come from my imagination, filling in the blanks and ignoring details of the actual game, which is sad really. 
I only buy the game for career mode, and honestly it really isn't worth it, there are too may things (I have touched on most of them above) that make the game stale and boring, and playing it because I USED to enjoy it, is starting to lose it's appeal. 

The worst part is, I feel that EA don't care about making a good game for career mode players, and I am sitting here writing this, instead of playing the game I grew up on and used to love. 

I would be so happy to pay money to play a career mode game with elements drawn from football manager in terms of realism, personality, transfer logic, play style.... If the gameplay stayed the same I could live with it, but if the career mode itself isn't renewed, and made better, I am done with the franchise completely.

I only bought EA FC 26 to play with a friend. I made the mistake of trying Career Mode again, and I genuinely don’t understand how EA managed to make it worse than last year.

This game does not feel fair — it feels scripted. Players take the ball off me while facing the wrong direction. Defenders magically catch my attackers no matter the pace stat or head start. Attributes don’t matter when the AI decides you’re not allowed to win.

The refereeing is beyond broken. In six hours of gameplay, I haven’t been awarded a single free kick. Not one. I get hacked, clipped, and shoved constantly with no call, while the AI gets away with everything. My defenders, meanwhile, seem allergic to marking, often running away from attackers like they’re afraid of the ball.

And then there’s the offside system. EA apparently thought it would be “realistic” to delay offside calls by 10 seconds. The game already knows I’m offside instantly — waiting to blow the whistle doesn’t add realism, it just kills momentum and reminds you you’re playing a poorly disguised simulation of football logic.

The most depressing part is that I want to enjoy this game. I force myself to boot it up because I just want a football game that’s actually fun. But the only way I can come close to enjoying myself is by lowering the difficulty — which completely removes any satisfaction from winning, lifting a trophy, or earning success. If the only way your game is enjoyable is by making it easier, something is fundamentally broken.

Once again, EA has delivered a product that feels less like a football game and more like a system designed to frustrate you just enough to keep you playing — or spending.

Final thought:
EA FC 26 isn’t made to be enjoyed — it’s made to be tolerated.

When that happens? No XP. No progression. No credit for the 70 minutes played, no recognition for goals scored, nothing. The time investment is completely wasted, and the game acts as if it never happened.

That’s not just poor optimization or “launch issues” — that’s a fundamentally broken product. Players are being asked to invest time, money, and loyalty into a system that cannot even guarantee basic match completion. For a competitive, online-focused football game, that failure is unforgivable.

What makes it worse is the disrespect it shows toward the sport itself. Football is the world’s game — passionate, technical, emotional. EA FC 26 does not reflect that legacy in any way. In its current state, it cheapens it. This game does not feel unfinished; it feels neglected, as if stability and player experience were secondary to monetization and yearly release deadlines.

This isn’t acceptable. Not from EA. Not at this scale. Not at this price.

I play mostly co-op with my friends and player and manager career modes.  

This game feels a lot like the old school Winning Eleven games and not in a good way.  Those games were graphically "simple" but the gameplay was god tier.  The best part about those games was you could edit them and make them so much prettier, edit player stats and appearance, change club kits, stadiums, languages.  To this day, anytime something bad happens, my friends and I say "where the f**k is Malgani(Maradona) when you need him?" 

EA Sports FC 26 feels like a half edited winning eleven game with so many bugs, it makes it almost unplayable.  It is definitely not enjoyable.  The offsides is a joke.  I say a joke to laugh because I want to cry it's so bad.  I have been called offsides several times and a good chunk of the defender's body(most of the time his ass or hip) is past the line they draw as offsides.  This has happened at least 6 or 7 times.  The difference between professional and world class difficulty levels, 1 level difference, is like the difference between playing soccer with kids and professionals respectively, in real life.  On Professional I beat teams like 9-0.  On World Class I can barely win 1-0.  Oh and if you want to see replays of your goals after they happen, I hope you like staring at the center circle.  Commentators are annoying and sound like we went back to 2004.  They are slow to react and the comments for some actions are just so out of place, like yelling when a defender gets the ball in their box even though there was no threat of goal.  Immersion is nonexistent.

I am glad I got it 60% off and I still overpaid.  This is basically a fancy launcher for FUT.  So if you don't play FUT or plan to play FUT, you are getting bent over and rammed repeatedly with that thing from Eurotrip, you know what I'm talking about, no matter what discount you are waiting for.

I don't do free to play games but at least it's free for players to get into it if they want to play online.  I am not saying it is any better but at least they don't make you pay a premium to get in. 

I am going back to not playing any soccer video games until a new contender comes in or Pachinkonami gets their heads outta their asses and brings back the best damn soccer video game series ever made.  EA Sports FC 26 is garbage.  This series is garbage.  Don't pay money for this dumpster full of garbage FUT launcher.

I was really excited for FC 26, but after spending enough time with the game, I can honestly say that it’s a disappointing experience. The biggest problem is the huge number of bugs and glitches that constantly break immersion and ruin gameplay. From broken animations and input delay to players behaving randomly, the game often feels unfinished.

Optimization is another major issue. Even on good hardware, the game struggles with performance. There are frequent frame drops, stuttering, and lag during matches, especially in intense moments. On top of that, the game freezes randomly, sometimes forcing a restart, which is extremely frustrating, especially during online matches.

The lag and delay make the gameplay feel unresponsive. Simple actions like passing, shooting, or switching players often happen late or not at all. This completely ruins the flow of the game and makes it feel unfair, as you’re fighting the controls more than your opponent.

What makes this even worse is that many of these problems have been present in previous versions, yet they remain unfixed. Instead of improving stability and performance, FC 26 feels like a rushed release with the same old issues carried over, along with new ones.

Overall, FC 26 has potential, but in its current state, it’s poorly optimized, unstable, and frustrating to play. Until the developers seriously address the bugs, glitches, lag, and freezing issues, I cannot recommend this game. It does not feel like a finished or polished product.

I buy FC every year with the same hope: this will be the one where Career Mode finally evolves.

And every year, I’m disappointed.

I don’t play Ultimate Team. I don’t care about online metas or packs. I play Career Mode — the offline, single-player experience that used to be the soul of football games.

But FC 26 feels like the same product… repackaged.

Yes, there are small tweaks. New menus. Minor UI changes. A feature here, a cutscene there. But when you actually play multiple seasons, the illusion fades fast. The same bugs. The same shallow mechanics. The same lack of immersion. Press conferences that don’t matter. Player development that feels scripted. AI behavior that hasn’t meaningfully evolved in years.

What hurts most isn’t that Career Mode is “bad.”
It’s that it’s stagnant.

Meanwhile, Ultimate Team gets constant attention, updates, events, and monetization hooks. Career Mode feels like it exists just so EA can say it wasn’t forgotten — not because it’s truly supported.

After paying full price year after year, I can’t shake the feeling that I’ve been bamboozled — sold hope instead of progress.

I don’t expect miracles. I don’t expect a revolution every year.
But I do expect respect for players who don’t engage with microtransactions and still love the sport.

If FC wants to keep career-only players, it needs to stop treating Career Mode as a checkbox and start treating it as a pillar again.

Until then, FC 26 isn’t a bad game.
It’s just a missed opportunity… again.

An absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for a FIFA/FC game. There are a lot of bugs that still haven’t been fixed. For example, in the social media section of Career Mode, the code sometimes confuses the main team with the transfer team.

What I mean is this: if your player is from Team A but a transfer rumour says he might move to Team B, most of the time the game switches it up. It ends up saying something like, “Player who grew up at Team B is rumoured to be moving to Team A,” even though your player is still at Team A.

Another issue in Career Mode or the game in general is the camera bug. Sometimes, if you score a goal and want to watch it again in the replay, you can’t, because the camera is somehow locked onto the halfway line.

The meta in FUT (Ultimate Team) is now fully reliant on midfield dominance. Formations that focus heavily on midfield play are the ones most commonly used by pros or RATs (e.g. 4-5-1 (2), 4-2-2-2, and 4-4-1-1 (2)). You see these formations constantly in Rivals and FUT Champs.

The reason for this is that attacking now relies almost entirely on AI positioning. From my experience playing the game and watching pro tactic videos, the typical approach is to trigger a run and then play a through ball. That’s essentially the only reliable way to win in this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. Another thing I’ve noticed while playing Rivals is how bad EA is at fixing mistakes when they fix one issue, it usually creates a new one.

For example, at one point a new scoring method was discovered where all you had to do was a rainbow flick and then press L2, and it would go in. If I’m not mistaken, this happened because EA removed goalkeeper movement. Now, after all the patches the game has gone through, the meta can be summed up perfectly by a Reddit comment I found:

“PlayStyles > body type > height > running & dribbling animations.
Stats matter for probabilities when you only have silver PlayStyles or for things that aren’t boosted by PlayStyles, such as AI movement and positioning, turning speed, and dribbling consistency.”

This is very accurate. Players without certain PlayStyles are labelled as “fodder” or “unusable,” regardless of how high their OVR or stats are. If they don’t meet the community’s definition of a meta or usable card, they’re instantly written off as fodder.

That said, I will admit that EA has at least slowed down the power curve.

This review is for the Career Mode, played on World Class on PC with keyboard. Simulation mode.

The game does have its moments. A brilliant pass or a fine combination leading to a goal gives a good vibe and in those moments the game seems like a true simulation of football.
But they are far and between, and the bulk of gameplay is utter rubbish. 
Attacking: 
Your players cannot dribble. And I dont mean some Messi dribbles. No, they cannot dribble a chair to save their lives. You try to change direction? They slow down or kick the ball to far. Or, most of the times, the defender gets some superhuman abilities to turn and accelerate and gets the ball. 
Passing is competent, but only thorough pass. Normal pass is slow like the player passing hasnt had anything to eat in days. Oh, and if the player passing isnt facing the intended receiver the pass is poor as f**k. 
Shooting is good only if there are no opponents between the shooter and goal, because if there are, no matter where you aim or the power you use, an opposing player will block the ball. Any ♥♥♥♥♥♥ time. On a positional attack, the CPU can easily play without a keeper. No shots will get past the defence.

Defending:
All the stuff I wrote above DO NOT apply to your defending. No matter their stats, your defenders will be slower, weaker and more stupid than the opposing attackers. Successful tackles are a matter of luck.
Adding to this, the AI controlled defenders are always far from their opponents and when the russian roulette that is player selection gives you control of them, they look like they just remembered where they are and what they're doing. Its that bad.
Oh, and pressing the key for "teammate contain" just gets another AI dumb drone to give moral support to the attacker. No tackling, no pressure, he just comes around to see if everything is ok. 
But to balance all this sh*t, the game gives your keeper the abilities of Spiderman. 17 years old keeper with a rating of 63 saves almost every shot, no matter the opponent, the distance or if the shooter was pressured or not.

Off the pitch:
For some unknown reason, almost all my players refuse to renew their contract. Old, young, good or bad, happy or unhappy, players are "not wiling to renew". I saw on the EA official page, A LOT of people asking to fix this. But it seems that EA does not care, and why should it? We already spent our money on this garbage. 
Having skipped EA FC 25, I saw that tactics got an "update" with the players getting a "role" ability. Except some "roles" making players position themselves in some ridiculous ways, this ability does f**k-all. 
The menus are ok, but why the hell did EA put another screen for the development of your players? On FC24 you went to Squad Hub, select a player and then select "Development" to set the training regime of your players. Now, selecting "Development" takes you to another screen where again you select the player you want to develop and only then you get to the types of training exercises. Why the hell? 
There is one good thing: now there is a job market for you as a coach that also lets you see the probability of getting to club you want as well as an option to set a "wishlist" of clubs you want to go to.
And another good thing: the academy and its Youth Tournaments are a good change, though they should accommodate tournaments for teams made out of more than 4 outfield players.

Visuals:
The game looks good, but that was to be expected. There are some visual bugs like players walking through the panels around the pitch or the camera for replays.

Conclusion:
The game could have been good if it was not made by EA. Maybe the online matches or the other modes are worth it, but Career Mode is an offence to the player. It is worth it only if you find it cracked on some torrent site.

I FOUND A SOLUTION for all pc/laptop gamers.....

I use a dual-monitor setup where my laptop screen is set as the primary display and monitor is used as the secondary display, when I launch Steam and start FC 26 on the secondary monitor, I MOVE my mouse cursor to the primary (laptop) screen before the game finishes loading, which prevents the game from defaulting to keyboard and mouse input and allows my Xbox controller (connected via Bluetooth) to be detected and work correctly.

My in-game display settings are set to 1920×1080 resolution at 165Hz, using either 30 FPS with VSync turned off or 60 FPS with VSync turned on, and with these settings the controller works properly, including in Seasons mode. the second setting ie 60fps usually does not work but 30fps settings 10000% works

There is a small issue where the game may start without sound because the mouse cursor is on the laptop screen ie primary display, but this is easily fixed by pressing Alt + Tab once, after which the sound returns immediately and the controller continues to function normally.

Once the game has fully loaded, you can move or use the mouse freely only on primary display and it will not affect controller gameplay on the secondary monitor; THE KEY POINT is that during the loading phase of FC 26, the mouse cursor must be on the primary (laptop) display, and if audio does not start, pressing Alt + Tab once resolves it.

Ive lost almost 30+ seasons match and more than 100+ hrs looking for solution but this works all the time...

Hopefully this helps anyone struggling with controller issues in FC 26 on a dual-monitor setup.

At launch, I genuinely believed this was one of the best iterations of the franchise in years. The gameplay felt balanced and rewarding. However, following recent updates, the experience has deteriorated so significantly that I now find it inferior to both FC24 and FC25.
​Gameplay & Defensive Mechanics

​The developer’s attempt to incorporate all community feedback has backfired. The defensive AI and manual tackling are currently at their worst. There is a glaring issue with skill-move scripting; it often feels as though the game "decides" a player will bypass the defense regardless of the defender’s positioning or timing. It has moved away from a skill-based simulation to an incredibly frustrating, inconsistent experience.

​Lack of Integrity and Moderation

​To test the reporting system, I documented several encounters with blatant cheaters. My experience with the "Anti-Cheat" system has been offensive:
​Inaction on Cheaters: I reported four hackers using the "unselectable player" exploit. After 21 days, I was matched against one of the same players again. It is clear that serious reports are being ignored.
​Automated Inconsistency: While my reports on actual hackers went nowhere, a "control" report I sent regarding a clean player received an immediate automated response.
​Final Verdict
​It is incredibly disappointing to see a game with so much potential be patched into such a poor state. The combination of broken defensive mechanics and a complete lack of effective moderation against hackers has made this unplayable.

​This will be the last title in the series I purchase. Thank you for taking a great game and making it a uniquely frustrating experience.

FC 26 feels like a yearly reminder that PC players are still treated as second-class citizens in EA’s ecosystem. No meaningful optimization improvements, no real performance focus, no signs that years of feedback were ever taken seriously. Stutters, inconsistent frame pacing, random input delay all of it is still here, untouched, like EA is preserving bugs as legacy features.

What makes it worse is that none of this is new. PC players have been reporting the same issues for multiple titles now, and FC 26 confirms one thing very clearly: EA hears the complaints, reads them, and then chooses to ignore them. The game runs like it’s permanently stuck in beta, yet we’re expected to treat it as a full priced AAA experience.

Now let’s address the topic EA desperately wants to pretend doesn’t exist anymore: Momentum, or as the community knows it, Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment. EA has released statements, explanations, and carefully worded excuses to make themselves look innocent, but FC 26 completely exposes the truth. The system is no longer subtle. In older games, at least you could doubt yourself. In FC 26, you don’t doubt anything you can literally feel when the game decides it’s not your turn to win.

The moment you enter Ultimate Team, skill becomes a suggestion rather than a rule. You can dominate possession, create clear chances, manually defend like your life depends on it, and still concede goals that feel scripted straight out of a bad comedy. Defenders suddenly forget how legs work, goalkeepers turn into training cones, and your perfectly timed tackles bounce back to the opponent like the ball is magnetized.

At that point, you’re not playing football anymore. You’re participating in a prewritten experience where the DDA system already chose the winner before kickoff. Your controller input just fills time between cutscenes.

Instead of addressing server quality, input responsiveness, PC optimization, or overall gameplay consistency, EA proudly delivers updates no one asked for. EA Play Music. Menu aesthetics. Cosmetic nonsense. The house is on fire, but EA is rearranging the playlist. Priorities are clear, and none of them involve improving how the game actually plays.

The lack of competition in the football game market is where everything truly falls apart. EA knows FC has no real rival, so there’s no pressure to innovate or improve. Players are given tiny drops of enjoyment just enough to stay hooked, while being hit with massive waves of frustration, grind, and monetization. Ultimate Team isn’t about football anymore, it’s a psychological endurance test designed to drain patience and wallets at the same time.

FC 26 feels less like a sports game and more like a live service experiment where fairness is optional and consistency is a luxury. Every match feels like flipping a coin, except the coin costs time and mental health.

In the end, until EA faces real competition, this cycle will continue, new title, same problems, louder marketing, and the same unanswered complaints.

Deeply Disappointed – EA FC 26 Still Doesn’t Listen to Its Community

After spending enough time with EA FC 26, I can honestly say it does not feel like the developers have listened to the community at all, despite constantly promoting that they have. The same long-standing issues continue to define the experience, and it’s frustrating to see nothing meaningful change.

The game still isn’t about skill, it's about who bought the strongest players. Especially in FUT events, newcomers stand no chance unless they invest hundreds of euros into better cards. This “pay-to-win” environment has only become worse, and it removes any sense of fairness or competitive integrity.

Pace is still overwhelmingly dominant. A weak player with 90+ pace will always reach the ball, outrun everyone, and score, no matter how well you defend or how skilled you actually are. It’s predictable, repetitive, and honestly just discouraging.

If EA insists on keeping expensive players in the game, then at least adjust the mechanics so that user skill matters more. For example, reduce how much the AI carries poor players and increase the demand for manual input. That way, even if someone buys top-tier players, the outcome will still depend on actual gameplay ability, not just on who spent the most money.

Right now, EA FC 26 feels like yet another step deeper into pay-to-win, not a step toward a better, more skill-based football game. And it’s a shame, because the community has been asking for the opposite for years.

Input responsiveness

Match fairness

Player experience in ranked modes

I have been wanting to write a review for this game for a long time, but honestly I do not even know where to begin. This franchise and the company behind it have made me feel a level of frustration and disappointment that I did not think a video game could cause. I am a competitive gamer. I have played at high levels in many different titles and I genuinely enjoy the challenge and the process of improving. But this game has tested my patience, my focus, and my love for competition more than anything I have ever played.

What I am about to explain is not just my personal experience. It is something that a huge part of the community feels as well.

Performance

Let us start with the most important issue which is performance. I can say this without hesitation. This is the worst performing and least responsive game I have ever played. The problem is not FPS issues, which many players already struggle with. The real problem is the constant, overwhelming input delay.

Around ninety percent of your time on this game is spent trying to fight through sluggish, sticky, delayed controls. You start wishing you could remember what true one to one input felt like because it is that rare. When the game suddenly becomes responsive, it actually feels shocking, like someone shining a torch into a cave you have been stuck in for weeks. The fact that this game claims to be competitive and that it even has an esport scene is genuinely hilarious. The game does not function at even a basic competitive standard.

Nothing, and I mean nothing, works consistently.

Mechanics

Mechanics are the next major problem because they define the skill ceiling of any competitive title. In this game you could play for three hundred hours and still struggle to find a single mechanic that works as intended. After thirty two years of making football games, this studio has not managed to create one reliably functional system. Except for the pack openings that generate absurd profits, of course. Those never break.

Continuing with the main gameplay mechanics:

AI

The AI is easily the most infuriating part of the entire game. In high intensity matches you quickly realise that you are not really playing against your opponent. You are playing against a team of scripted robots that read the game better than any human possibly could.

High division players barely defend manually anymore. They do not need to. Second man press auto tackles for them. AI controlled defenders mirror your movements perfectly. At random moments the AI will decide that you are a threat and take the ball from you even when your opponent has done absolutely nothing.

It is a complete crutch for players who have no defensive skill and it has made matches feel fraudulent for months. The community has complained constantly and nothing has been done.

Passing

Passing is an absolute disaster. You are genuinely scared to build an attack because at any moment the game might send a pass in a direction you never intended. Passes can go ninety degrees off or one hundred and eighty degrees off. Sometimes the game ignores the three players in the area you aimed at and instead sends the ball across the entire pitch to someone behind a defender.

It is unpredictable. It is unreliable. It ruins the flow of the game.

Tackling

Tackling is just as bad. You can read a play perfectly, block the lane, win the ball cleanly and immediately watch it bounce straight back to your opponent. Not once, not twice, but sometimes three or four times in a row. Usually this happens in high pressure moments and often leads directly to goals.

It completely kills any feeling of control you thought you had.

Switching

Right stick switching feels like gambling. You flick the stick and pray. It might switch to the player you intended or it might jump to someone across the pitch and instantly cost you a goal. The LB or L1 switching that is supposed to select the player with the small cursor indicator simply does not work. It constantly switches to anyone except who you need in the moment.

It feels inconsistent, unpredictable and random in the worst ways.

Updates

This is the saddest part. For the first couple of weeks the game actually had the highest skill ceiling we have seen in years. It was still flawed but it was playable and mostly fair.

Then the updates arrived. Each one chipped away at the gameplay until it became a mess again. Every patch made things worse and pushed the game further from skill based competition.

Final Verdict

I have barely scratched the surface of the issues this game has. These are only the most obvious problems and there are many more. As for whether it is worth buying, the answer for me is very simple. No. Absolutely not. I will never play or recommend this franchise to anyone again. It is incompetence mixed with greed and a complete lack of respect for players or their time.

I mainly play Career Mode, which in FC26 has been lovingly redesigned to answer one question:

“What if the AI was allowed to be Manchester City on steroids, and you were allowed to be… a traffic cone?”

World Class difficulty?
More like World Class Torture Simulator.

The AI now passes the ball with such divine precision that I’m convinced they mo-capped actual deities. I can’t even get close. I’m pressing, jockeying, sprinting, praying, and the AI just casually strings together 47 one-touch passes like they’re running a training drill. Meanwhile, my players receive the ball like it’s a live grenade.

Defending?
Forget it. The moment I try to close the gap, the AI slips in another laser pass straight through three players who apparently forgot they have legs. It’s like playing against 11 prime Iniestas while I control 11 shopping trolleys with low battery wheels.

Attacking?
Fair. Balanced. Totally realistic.
As long as “realistic” means every goalkeeper has suddenly become the second coming of Buffon.

I love Career Mode, but EA 26 has turned it into a philosophical experience.
Not fun, but deeply reflective.

Questions I now ask myself daily:

Why can the AI dribble through five players, but I lose the ball if someone breathes in my direction?

Why is World Class basically Ultimate wearing a fake moustache?

Why is passing so clean for the AI and so… potato for me?

In summary:
If you enjoy watching the AI play beautiful football while you run around like a lost Labradoodle, this is GOTY material.

If you want a balanced Career Mode?
Just put your controller down and watch the CPU vs CPU matches.
It’s the only way you’ll see your team win.

But it’s impossible to appreciate that when you can’t complete a full match without holding your breath and hoping the game doesn’t implode.

Performance issues aren’t just occasional annoyances—they’re the entire experience. Crashes happen so regularly that troubleshooting becomes a bigger part of the game than scoring goals. Whether it’s poor optimization, lack of proper testing, or simply rushed development, the end result is the same: EA FC Sports 26 feels unfinished and borderline unplayable on PC.

Unless these issues are fixed with serious updates, it’s hard to recommend this game to anyone. Right now, it’s less a football simulation and more a crash simulator—and an extremely frustrating one at that.

I have played this game for a little over 195 hours, focusing almost entirely on Career Mode, as I generally avoid online modes like FUT due to EA’s servers feeling unstable at times. From an offline perspective, EA FC 26 delivers strong presentation, improved animations, and enjoyable gameplay when everything functions as intended.

However, as you progress deeper into Manager Career Mode, more unresolved bugs begin to appear. Contract negotiations often behave incorrectly — for example, players requesting extensions despite still having four years remaining on their deals, or demanding unrealistically high salaries without performance justification. On top of that, AI behavior can be inconsistent, tactical instructions may not apply properly, cutscenes become repetitive, and simulation or transfer logic can break immersion. These issues don’t make the mode unplayable, but they do highlight a lack of refinement for offline-focused players.

Despite these shortcomings, this is still the best football game available today, and for that reason alone, there is no justification for giving it a harsh rating.

Score: 3/5 – A solid experience, though Career Mode clearly needs more attention and stability improvements.

FC 26 launched with a strong foundation and delivered an enjoyable experience right from the start. The gameplay felt smooth, engaging, and full of potential. While there were a few issues—such as corner glitches and several minor bugs—these were problems that could have been resolved with targeted patches.

However, the direction of the recent updates has been disappointing. Because the community has been vocal and divided, often “crying” from both sides about every small aspect of the game, the developers’ response has led to changes that feel reactionary rather than thoughtful. As a result, the last few updates have noticeably impacted the balance and overall quality of gameplay, to the point where it feels like the game has been altered for the worse.

Another concern is player-card balancing. Some of the female cards currently feel unrealistically strong compared to many male cards, which creates a sense of imbalance during matches. To be clear, I mean absolutely no disrespect—I fully respect women, and representation in games is important. But within the context of FC 26’s gameplay, the tuning and stats don’t always feel consistent or fair, and at times it gives the impression that the balancing is leaning more heavily in favor of the female player base. The result is a competitive experience that doesn’t always feel even or authentic.

I genuinely hope the developers take a step back and reassess the direction of future updates. FC 26 had great potential at launch, and with careful balancing and more measured adjustments, it could return to being the enjoyable, well-rounded experience it once was.

UPDATED review to reflect the game as of 11/01/26:


The game is full of bugs, including (but not limited to):

- Never ending pause menus (you're lucky if you can get through half-time and play the second half - same with post-match interviews!)

- Code-related errors (including the amazing feature of in-game commentary only displaying goal scorer's first name)

- More code-related errors (International job offers show as "CM_TASK_mumbo-jumbo", rather than showing the actual job offer or national side)

- Labyrinth of a main menu (want to find Manager Mode, Exhibition, or anything other than Ultimate Team? Good luck jumping through many hoops finding them!)

- Enjoying your career mode save? Saves will randomly corrupt... sometimes after a few games, sometimes after a few seasons.

As for features, this game includes some revolutionary points, including:

- Being sacked regardless of season performance, for simming matches and/or failing to answer the same questions before/after every match in the interviews.

- Majority of deflections and goalkeeper saves going straight to the AI opponent players.

- Substituted players with more stamina being outpaced by AI opponent players who've played over 60 minutes of the match.

- Headers so soft, it's like the devs are afraid the player models will get CTE. Defensive headers have power, attacking headers are weaker than passing gas on the ball.

- Assisted passing sometimes goes in a complete different direction, plays the wrong type of pass, or goes straight to the AI opponent.

- Player-controlled players won't intercept AI opponent passes, even if it's practically rolling over their feet. AI opponent players attract the ball like it's made of steel, and their boots are magnets.

- Global transfers are reported on during every match. You can hear about how an Azerbaijani Under-18 has transferred to a Polish relegation club - and it'll be reported as if it's a World Cup winner moving to a Top-5 club.

The worst part of all, is this is the first EAFC/FIFA title I've played since FIFA 23 - and it's somehow gone backwards! Hopefully now Saudi Arabia have bought EA, they'll pay the money to get this circus properly sorted (as well as more than 30 national teams to play as)!

I seldom write reviews for any games but this time I feel like I need to.

Cons:
- First week of the game was actually pretty good. Most of the issues EA addressed during their promo video pre-release of the game was actually there. Ball retention after a tackle was better. Fewer bounce backs. Smarter goal keeper positioning and more nuanced ways to pass and attack with the ball. Fast forward to 2-3 patches after? All gone. In fact its somehow even worse than FC25 AT ITS WORST!

-Attacking AI is horrible. The game does not promote tactical creativity. This is in both Career mode and Ultimate team. It feels like there is only one correct way to play the game and any other formation is just there so EA can say hey we gave you options. Even if you are using the "Meta" formation it doesn't matter. If you do not have the players then it still doesn't work. Yes I am talking to you Claudia Pina enjoyers out there...... There is no authentic movement. There is no use having the attacking positioning stat because players will not occupy space or do any off the ball movement without me player locking or spamming runs or trying to flick every single player into positions they should naturally find themselves in.

-Rewards. At my peak I was consistently a Div 1 - Elite player from FIfa 23-25. I am not here to say I am great at the game. I grinded alot and eventually found a consistent formation with several players I really gel with. Pack weight and luck has always been hit or miss but its nice to occasionally pack someone worthwhile and try to fit them into my team. This year, the rewards are meaningless. The promos make 0 sense its as if EA are watching football upside down. The rewards for everything are terrible. The cards are meaningless. Even if you pack a card that looks great on paper it does not translate one bit onto the pitch. There is no motivation to try new cards or new formations because there are only a handful of "correct" cards you should play with. Nothing else.

-Animations. Wow... I don't even know where to start. Adding animations on top of broken animations to break something that is already broken. Not much to say here but, how can Fifa 10,11,12 have more authentic looking animations than this game? Any sort of animation is broken. Goalkeepers attempting saves with t-rex arms. Defenders lifting their legs slightly to go into a tackle. Strikers kicking at nothing and tripping over themselves for the fun of it. Stop adding animations and fix the existing ones that have been broken since FC 24.

-Playstyles. I truly believe playstyles ruined the game. This was just another greedy way for EA to sell you "useable" cards. Why do I say this? Because without playstyles you cannot do the most simple pass. Without incisive, the through ball is a direct pass to the opponent. Without anticipate your defender attempts a tackle in the opposite direction of the opponent. Without quick step or rapid, it does not matter if your player has 90+ pace, regardless of whatever body type. They will not run. If you pay attention to promo releases, EA will deliberately save cards with "useable" playstyles during TOTY or TOTS or FUTTIES. Just so they can squeeze an extra buck out of you. Playstyles have ruined the game. I truly do not believe a professional footballer that gets paid thousands a week cannot make a simple through ball without having "incisive". I am not even talking about to break the defence with one pass. 

TLDR: This is a nothing game. Canadians should not be allowed to make a football game. Stick to Hockey please. Or some lumberjack simulation game where the reward is a large jug of maple syrup.

EA Sports FC 26 Review: The Beautiful Game, Split

Score: 8.0/10

EA Sports FC 26 is more than just an annual update; it's a critical recalibration for the franchise, successfully addressing years of community feedback by introducing a fundamental and, at times, divisive change to its core gameplay. By splitting the on-pitch action into two distinct presets—Competitive and Authentic—EA Vancouver has managed to cater to both its demanding esports audience and those who crave a more realistic, methodical football simulation. While monetization issues persist, the sheer quality of the on-pitch experience makes this the strongest entry since the series reboot.

Dual Identity: Competitive vs. Authentic Gameplay

The headline feature of FC 26 is its dual gameplay system, which is arguably its greatest success and most notable risk.

Competitive Mode: This is the default for online modes like Ultimate Team and Clubs. It is tuned for speed, responsiveness, and quick reflexes. Dribbling and player movement feel incredibly snappy, thanks to an overhauled Dynamic Dribbling system that provides faster jog dribbles and sharper directional changes. Goalkeepers here are smarter about deflecting danger to wide areas, reducing the pinball goals that plagued previous titles. This mode is a high-octane thrill ride, rewarding those who master skill moves and lightning-fast counter-attacks.

Authentic Mode: Designed for Career Mode and offline play, this mode is a revelation for simulation purists. The tempo is slower, player positioning is more intelligent, and the ball physics feel heavier and less "arcadey." Defensive positioning is significantly improved, and the new Manager Live Challenges in Career Mode truly benefit from this realistic approach, creating genuine tactical battles.

The choice is a game-changer, allowing players to tailor the experience to their specific session goals. However, the feeling that you are playing two separate games prevents a perfect score, as some wish the competitive mode would embrace realism just a little more.

Mode Evolution: FUT, Clubs, and Career

Beyond the pitch, FC 26 delivers meaningful, if uneven, updates across its tentpole modes.

Football Ultimate Team (FUT) remains the engine of the game, receiving crucial accessibility improvements. The removal of Champions Playoffs and the expansion of Champions Ranks (from 10 to 15 tiers) lowers the barrier to entry, making participation feel more rewarding for the average player. New Tournaments and Live Events add welcome variety to the grind. Unfortunately, the increased emphasis on microtransactions and the clumsy integration of women’s players into the system remain major points of friction for the community.

Clubs benefits massively from the introduction of the new Archetype system. This allows for deep, individualized player progression inspired by real-life greats, giving each Pro a distinct feel on the pitch. The ability to affiliate with multiple clubs and the addition of Rush-style 5v5 matches adds flexibility and fun to the social experience.

Career Mode sees a much-needed injection of unpredictability with the Manager Live Challenges and a dynamic coaching market. These features introduce alternative story lines and realistic, mid-season tactical shifts, ensuring that each season feels fresh and challenging.

Presentation and Authenticity

FC 26 continues to deliver market-leading visual fidelity. The Frostbite engine shines, especially with the introduction of new volumetric goalkeeper animations that lend an unprecedented level of realism to shot-stopping. The licensing remains comprehensive, featuring over 20,000 players, 750 clubs, and exclusive rights to the UEFA competitions. The presentation package is polished, with improved player likenesses and cleaner UI across the board.

Verdict

EA Sports FC 26 is an excellent football game that finally gives its community what it has been asking for: choice. The split gameplay engine successfully services two very different needs—the adrenaline rush of competitive online play and the tactical satisfaction of a realistic simulation.

While the perennial issues of aggressive monetization in Ultimate Team and some optimization hiccups prevent it from being a legendary entry, the innovations in Career Mode and the quality of the on-pitch football in both modes make EA FC 26 a must-buy for any fan of the sport. It's a game with two halves, and both are playing at an elite level.

Pros:

Dual gameplay modes (Competitive & Authentic) dramatically improve player choice.

Authentic Mode offers the best pure football simulation in the series history.

Overhauled dribbling and player movement feel responsive and fluid.

Archetype system revitalizes Clubs and Player Career progression.

Cons:

Continued focus on aggressive monetization in Football Ultimate Team.

Online stability and optimization still need minor patches.

The "two-games-in-one" approach might feel slightly disjointed.

The game is completely unstable in online modes. The controller suffers from constant input delay, random freezes, and even full disconnections during matches. What makes it worse is that this issue happens ONLY in this game—every other game on my PC runs perfectly fine. Offline modes work normally, but the moment you try to play online, the gameplay becomes unplayable.

I’ve tried every possible fix: reinstalling the game, updating drivers, changing USB cables, checking network settings, verifying files, adjusting graphics options—you name it. Nothing solves the problem. My PC meets all the recommended specs, so hardware is not the issue.

It’s extremely disappointing to pay for a game where the main feature—online play—doesn’t work at all. EA FC 26 feels rushed, poorly optimized, and not ready for PC players. Until these serious technical problems are fixed, I honestly cannot recommend this game to anyone.

I want to share my experience so others know what to expect.
EA Sports FC 26 has serious performance problems that appear randomly, even on decent hardware.

In my case, the game runs well at first, and I can easily get high FPS in menus or during the first match. But after playing one match, the performance suddenly collapses for no reason. FPS drops to 20–30 during gameplay, animations stutter, and everything becomes extremely laggy. Restarting the game sometimes helps temporarily, but the issue always returns after the next match.

I’ve tried everything:
– updating GPU drivers
– cleaning cache and shaders
– switching between DX11 and DX12
– disabling V-Sync
– checking temperatures (which are normal)
– repairing or reinstalling the game

Nothing provides a permanent fix.
It feels like the game breaks its own performance after each match, even though no settings are changed.

Considering the price of the game, these stability issues are unacceptable. Until EA addresses and fixes this problem, I cannot recommend FC 26.

I have played this game for a little over 40 hours, focusing almost entirely on Career Mode, as I generally avoid online modes like FUT due to EA’s servers feeling unstable at times. From an offline perspective, EA FC 26 delivers strong presentation, improved animations, and enjoyable gameplay when everything functions as intended.

However, as you progress deeper into Manager Career Mode, more unresolved bugs begin to appear. Contract negotiations often behave incorrectly for example, players requesting extensions despite still having four years remaining on their deals, or demanding unrealistically high salaries without performance justification. On top of that, AI behavior can be inconsistent, tactical instructions may not apply properly, cutscenes become repetitive, and simulation or transfer logic can break immersion. My Honest Review of EA Sports FC 26 After the Latest Update:

Honestly, the previous update was way better in terms of AI behavior and realism. The opponents used to play according to their team quality — stronger teams felt organized and dangerous, while weaker teams were more balanced and realistic. That variety made the gameplay fun, immersive, and authentic.

After the latest update, though, the AI feels completely broken. Now every team plays like prime Brazil 2002, and every player turns into Messi. There’s no difference between small clubs and top-tier teams anymore — everyone dribbles perfectly, never misses passes, and constantly pulls off unrealistic moves.

Even worse, the gameplay has become way too negative and boring. The AI keeps passing the ball backwards, holding possession for no reason, instead of trying to attack or win. It’s frustrating and kills the whole experience.

It feels like the developers are listening to a very small portion of the community, ignoring the majority of players who prefer realistic, competitive, and enjoyable football.
As someone who mainly plays offline Career Mode as a manager, I want to experience football that feels real — not a game where the AI just passes around endlessly like it’s trying to waste time.

Honestly, I really hope EA reconsiders the direction they’re taking. The previous version had much better balance, realism, and fun. Right now, it just feels disappointing and not enjoyable at all.

FC 26 Summary Review: An Unfinished and Frustrating Product
I am writing this review with deep frustration. FC 26, especially the PC version, is one of the worst games I have ever played. The experience is defined by a mountain of bugs, repetitive gameplay, and persistent technical issues that make it unbearable.
Technical Flaws and EA's Useless "Fix"
The most critical problem is the technical instability. The community widely reports severe input lag on PC. EA themselves acknowledged the issues, advising players to lock the game at 60 FPS and enable V-Sync. However, this "fix" is a sham because the game fails to save these settings, forcing you to re-apply them constantly. To make matters worse, the controls sometimes randomly switch to keyboard and mouse, adding another layer of frustration.
Monotonous Gameplay and Impossible Defending
On the pitch, the gameplay is just as disappointing. Tactics are useless, as the game boils down to exploiting the same predictable attacking moves. Defending is powerless: even when you read the opponent's play and position your defender perfectly, the ball often phases through them as if they weren't there. In contrast, the opponent's AI defenders intercept passes with frustrating ease, even in open space. Ball possession is also a joke; even after a successful tackle, the attacker frequently recovers the ball instantly.
Goalkeepers and Finishing: Inverted Logic
Goalkeeping and finishing are absurd. Simple, weak low driven shots aimed directly at the keeper often go in, while well-placed, powerful shots are saved with superhuman ability. This inverted logic destroys the satisfaction of scoring a well-crafted goal and makes the game's physics feel broken.
The Crossplay Divide and Broken Mechanics
There is a clear disadvantage for PC players in crossplay. Console opponents execute moves that are simply not possible on PC due to the input lag. The meta is ridiculous: defend deep because the AI intercepts everything, then launch a counter-attack with a fast player who can use quick, unrealistic direction changes that defenders can't counter. Even when you anticipate the move, the attacker often glitches through. The refereeing is also inconsistent, ignoring blatant fouls, and defenders can make impossible tackles from behind.
Conclusion: A Rip-Off
FC 26 is an unfinished, broken product. The number of bugs and poor gameplay make you feel cheated. It's not worth it. Do not play this game. I feel completely ripped off and want my money back. Many of the complaints and problems I report here can be found echoed across community forums, such as Reddit and EA's own support pages.

Давайте будем честны: если вы ждете революции, вас ждет разочарование. "FC26" — это не новая игра, а мастерски сделанный патч для прошлогодней версии. И это одновременно его главная сила и слабость.

Что нравится: Эволюция, а не революция:

1. "На поле" играть стало приятнее. Разработчики снова поработали над физикой мяча и движения игроков. Пасы стали чуть более упругими, отскоки — чуть менее предсказуемыми, а дриблинг требует большего чувства времени. Первые несколько часов ощущается свежесть, кажется, что вы открываете футбол заново.
2. Визуальная составляющая на высоте. Лица игроков, текстуры газона, освещение на стадионах — все это на уровне голливудской графики. В режиме "Карьера" во время трансферов кат-сцены выглядят как кадры с реального ТВ. Иммерсивность зашкаливает.

3. Обновленные составы и лицензии. Это, пожалуй, главная причина для покупки для многих. Играть с актуальным составом своей любимой команды, в новой форме и с правильными игроками — бесценно. Появление нескольких новых полностью лицензированных лиг тоже радует.

4.  Моддинг (на ПК). Если вы играете на ПК, то "FC26" для вас — бесконечный конструктор. Сообщество моддеров исправляет все огрехи разработчиков: добавляет недостающие лицензии, лица, бутсы, мячи и стадионы. Фактически, через пару месяцев после выхода игра становится идеальной в плане антуража.

Что разочаровывает: Год за годом одно и то же.

1. Ощущение "дежавю". После 10-15 часов игры приходит понимание, что вы уже проходили это. Тот же самый ИИ соперника, который действует по шаблону. Те же самые баги в анимации, когда вратарь проваливается в текстуры, а защитники сталкиваются друг с другом. Создается впечатление, что исправляют одни старые баги, но добавляют столько же новых.

2.  Ультимативная Команда (FUT/Dream Team) — кошелек или громадная рутина. Режим, который приносит больше всего денег, снова заточен под микротранзакции. Шансы получить по-настоящему классного игрока без вложений реальных денег стремятся к нулю. Вы либо платите, либо тратите нездоровое количество времени на бесконечный гринд.

3.  Режим "Карьера" снова обделен вниманием. Добавили пару новых диалогов, пару новых фотокарточек в новостное дайджество, пару новых тумблеров в начале создания карьеры, новая фича "Случайные обстоятельства". При этом фундаментальные проблемы — дурацкий ИИ при трансферах, нереалистичное развитие молодых игроков, однотипные задания от руководства — все осталось на месте. Кажется, этот режим существует по инерции.

4.  Серверы и баги в день релиза. Традиция, которая не нарушается. В первые дни поиграть онлайн почти невозможно: лаги, разрывы соединений, ошибки загрузки. Ощущение, что компания снова не была готова к наплыву игроков.

Вердикт

"FC26" — это комфортный, но дорогой апгрейд.

Стоит покупать, если: Вы заядлый фанат, который следит за обновлениями составов, регулярно играет онлайн и пропустил прошлогоднюю версию. Вы получите ровно то, что ожидаете: красивый и плавный футбольный симулятор с актуальными данными. Не стоит покупать (или подождать до скидок), если: Вы обладатель прошлогодней версии и вас устраивает геймплей. Вы в основном играете в офлайн-режимы вроде "Карьеры". Нововведения не стоят тех полных 70-80 долларов, которые просят на старте.

Итог: "FC26" — это качественный продукт, но он давно уже не является "игрой года". Это надежный, предсказуемый ежегодный ритуал для фанатов футбола. Он дает вам ровно столько, чтобы вы купили его снова через год, но не больше.

FC 26 is a strong and enjoyable step forward for the series, offering noticeable improvements over FC 25 in almost every major area. While it might not be the best football game ever made, it delivers a balanced, polished, and entertaining experience that feels more complete and rewarding than last year’s entry.

Gameplay feels smoother and more realistic than in FC 25. Passing and shooting have better weight, dribbling is more responsive, and defending feels fair and skill-based. Matches flow naturally, with fewer awkward animations and more variety in how goals are scored. The improved ball physics make every game feel unique and competitive.

Career Mode has also been refined. Player development is more dynamic, training and performance matter more, and manager career offers deeper tactical options and smarter AI. It feels less repetitive than in FC 25 and gives players a genuine sense of progress and control over their team’s future. Player Career continues to grow as well, with better customization and feedback systems that make climbing through the ranks satisfying.

Visually, FC 26 looks excellent. Lighting, stadiums, and player faces have all been upgraded. The crowd atmosphere and broadcast-style presentation make each match feel alive. Compared to FC 25, menus are smoother, animations are cleaner, and overall presentation is more consistent.

The soundtrack and commentary are both strong, helping create a lively atmosphere that matches the energy on the pitch. Online play feels more stable, with fewer delays and smoother matchmaking, making it more enjoyable for competitive players.

FC 26 may not reinvent the franchise, but it clearly builds on what FC 25 lacked. It’s a more confident, fluid, and rewarding football game that focuses on refining the experience rather than forcing unnecessary changes.

Final Verdict: FC 26 is a major improvement over FC 25 and one of the most enjoyable football titles in years. It plays better, looks better, and feels more authentic. Definitely worth buying for anyone who loves the sport.

After 127 hours of gameplay, I can say that this is a completely different game compared to any of its predecessors. Let’s start with the gameplay, as the most important aspect. In short — it’s much more realistic than ever before, but there’s still room for improvement.

When it comes to competitive gameplay, the first thing you notice is that defending is much harder for two reasons. First, you can no longer just keep spamming the tackle button until your player wins the ball. Second, the over-the-top agility of players makes defending much more difficult — but I’ll get to that in a moment.

Another thing is that there are no weird ball deflections or so-called “scripts.” Passes are not as inaccurate as in EA FC 25, but not every pass will be perfect either. Players will rarely make an accurate pass under pressure, while passes are extremely precise when the player is not under pressure. If a pass is made while turning or from a difficult position, the chances of success are very low. On the other hand, if the player is calm and not pressed, even harder passes tend to go through — which adds a lot of realism, even in competitive play.

Shots under pressure are quite inaccurate, which again adds realism. Goalkeepers have been improved — they’re not unbeatable, but they finally feel realistic, not terrible like in previous FIFAs. So far, I haven’t noticed any goalkeeper glitches like before, which is great.

What I don’t like in competitive gameplay is the excessive agility, especially of female players, which makes defending almost impossible. An opponent who knows how to play will just keep moving left and right until they break through and score. This is a big issue and I hope agility gets toned down in future updates — not only because it’s unrealistic, but also because it makes defending frustrating.

Chip shots are also overpowered — it doesn’t matter whether a player has the “chip shot” playstyle or not, they’ll still lob your goalkeeper from 30 meters with insane precision if you rush out. I really dislike that. On the bright side, finesse shots and long-range trivela shots no longer work, so you won’t be seeing goals from 30+ meters anymore. Thank God green-timed shots were removed — huge thumbs up to EA for that.

Lastly, and very importantly, it seems that anticheat is working well so far — I haven’t encountered any cheaters yet, though there’s still time; the season is long.

When it comes to Authentic gameplay, things are much better overall, but there’s still room for fixes. Weather effects like wind, rain, and snow are amazingly realistic — players can actually slip on wet grass or snow — and the gameplay is much slower and more realistic than in competitive mode.

The only problem for me is that even on the hardest difficulty (Ultimate), I can still beat the AI pretty easily, so Authentic gameplay needs to be made a bit tougher. The AI is definitely dumber here than in Competitive mode.

Career Mode is much more interesting now thanks to the new random events and the manager market, although the rest hasn’t changed much compared to previous EA FC games. The lack of national teams and perhaps a few more leagues is disappointing — I know that’s due to licensing issues, but national teams are sorely missed.

Finally, let’s talk about graphics. The graphics are stunning — easily the best in the series so far. The detail in ball deflections off the goalkeeper’s fingers, the realistic movement of kits — everything makes this game look better than ever.

However, there’s a small issue that still persists, though it’s getting better with every update. I’ve experienced input delay and occasional stuttering during online matches (especially in Ultimate Team), like after corners or pauses. It used to be very irritating, but it’s much improved now, making the game far more playable.

I play on a Ryzen 5700X and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060, with very fast internet, so this shouldn’t be happening — I’ve played much more demanding games on Ultra settings without any lag or FPS drops.

All in all, to sum up — I’d rate this game an 8/10, and I’d gladly give it a perfect 10/10 if the issues mentioned above get fixed. This is probably the best game in the series so far, and I truly hope EA continues to listen to the fans and make EA FC as realistic as possible.

EAFC: When Football Stopped Rewarding Skill

Review:

I’ve played every FIFA since 1996, and I’ll say this straight — FIFA 12 was the last great one. It was the perfect balance between realism, control, and pure skill. Every pass, tackle, and goal felt earned. You could dominate someone because you were genuinely better — smarter with your buildup, cleaner with your timing, sharper with your positioning.

Since FIFA 13 & Getting worse every year, the series has lost that. EAFC isn’t skill-based anymore — it’s random, automated, and often feels scripted. Player control and responsiveness fluctuate from game to game. You can read your opponent perfectly and still get punished because the game “decides” otherwise. It’s like skill doesn’t matter; it’s about who gets the next momentum swing.

And the worst part? EA has made it impossible for any real competition to exist. Their stranglehold on football licenses — leagues, kits, stadiums, and players — means nobody else can build a proper alternative. Some try, but without those official rights, it can’t truly compete. So we’re stuck with a monopoly that no longer values gameplay integrity.

EAFC looks incredible, sure. But under the surface, it’s a hollow experience — a football game that forgot what made it great. For long-time players who loved the tactical chess match of FIFA 10–12, this new era feels like watching your favorite sport turn into a casino.

Verdict:

Let me start by saying that I am the casual player for this game. I play specifically player campaign and thats it. No casino. No multiplayer with sweats. Good old fashion single player. Also keep in mind I haven't played a FIFA game since 2013 so this is all new to me.

- Difficulty -
Play on Professional if you want an okay challenge but still want to run the game over. AI on professional is just bad enough where you can run at the guy during kickoff and steal the ball and go all the way and score. If you dont do that it's still bad but takes a bit of work but not much.
Play on World Class for just the right difficulty. You need to work for your goals but the AI is still not good but this time its on your team. This difficulty is rough if you are playing as your own character only. On this difficulty you also have to deal with defenders who are always faster than whoever is dribbling. There are no breakaways even on a through ball. Even if you do perfect "dribble-ons" or whatever they are called. You will always get caught.

- AI -
The AI likes to try to pass to you ALL THE TIME. even if its straight into the opponent. I can't count how many times in a single game where my team will just try to pass to me when I am defended by 3 guys and I get rating down because I lost possession. Or they just straight up pass it to the opponent. And if it can't find a path to you, it will just slowly dribble to the sideline and then pass it to the opponent.
On the flip side, the opponent AI (on world class) will pass in triangles, use cross passes, run down the sideline while my defenders just let them go all the way down. Their ball movement is just so much better because it doesn't have to worry about trying to satisfy the player always getting the ball. Its extremely frustrating when I see their teamwork and my team is just trying to feed me in a bad way.
Overall, AI needs work. At times it feels good and challenging but mostly its bad.

- Player Career Training -
This doesn't matter. Pick two heavy trainings to get A ratings in and just simulate them before every game. It doesn't do anything but give you player XP boosts for each game. And as long as you do it like this, you get the max XP for the training every game as well as never can go below starting 11 when get achieve it (after the second game).
Horrible system. Not satifying. Should be removed from the game for tutorials.

- Personality -
Horrible system. Choices don't really matter after you get started. And its not really explained well at all. Perks are cool that they are tied to you personality but could just be done better. Nothing else to really say.

- Personality Challenges -
In game challenges that give you personality points scale pretty hard early so if you are playing on a higher difficulty they will become harder to achieve which is fine until they as for 3-4 goals on your specific player and you are happy to get 1-2. 10.0 rating on a challenge is only achievable when you get an unrealistic scoreline so don't expect to do that one every game. Others are really doable like 30% dibble accuracy or just take 3 shots on net.
All in all, either too easy or not possible on hard difficulties.

- Overall -
Game is fine. It scratches the itch after not playing these games for a long time. Lots of flaws that can be patched. Probably won't because small indie company. When I look past the poor AI for player career its fun.
