This review is coming from someone who has DOMINATED Ultimate Team since FIFA13, but you can still take it with a grain of salt if you'd like.

First off, is the game better than FC25? In some aspects, it is: faster and more dynamic gameplay, better player movement, skills can actually be pulled off (because of one of the negatives) and the power curve of the players in UT is not as high as it used to be in the previous games. The only people you will hear complaing about this last part are the cash cows that want to have the best team from day 1.

Now to talk about the bad things and all of those really piss me off.
The AI awareness for defending and attacking is absolutely pathetic. During an attack, my players would just be walking backwards or sideways and look at me instead of doing runs between the defense (and that's with either Poacher++ or Advanced Forward++). Same goes for the defense. If the player doesnt have Intercept as a trait, the ball will literally pass a centimeter away from them and they won't react to cut it and a lot of people abuse that.
But the one thing that pisses me off the most is how they've ruined the defending in this title. I have never seen the standing tackle being so worthless in any of the FIFA games that I've played so far. It is ABYSMAL! Literally to the point where I only use it like 7-8 times per game MAX. The rest of the time, I run around using my CDMs trying to cover gaps for passes and rely on the AI to defend with my CBs. The moment you touch one of your CBs, you're done. In FC24 and FC25, the defending was really well done imo and there was no reason to change it, but EA has decided to completely screw it up. If it doesnt get patched, then prepare for a bad experience overall this year...

I have been playing Fifa for more than a decade (all the psp, ps3, ps4 games) mainly in career mode. I have skipped fc25 because the gameplay felt so bad from the 10 hour trial. Coming back to this game after a year, these are my opinions on it:

Pros:
-Fluid passing
-Smooth dribbling
-Shooting feels nice (thanks for bringing back the low driven)
-I love the tactics in this game, and they feel like they matter a lot.
-UI has greatly improved
-Unexpected events in career has been a great addition

Cons:
-The physics of the ball in the air are so unrealistic and bad, this includes crossing, ball control in the air, headers, ball trajectory, lobbed through passes, etc.
-Sprinting with the ball tends to push the ball forward a lot after two touches
-PC performance during corners and cutscenes and replays is bad, although has been improved by update 1.0.3
-Career mode has a glitch where if a player requests to leave and they get automatically put on the transfer list, they cannot be sold as all offers are rejected automatically.
-Some menus are unintuitive. Choosing to load your career mode save from the main menu is very hard, as  the options under manager career are confusing.
-Playing against the AI is not a pleasant experience; authentic sliders make the cpu very easy, with lots of spaces in behind and slow build up and no fouls. Changing the sliders around tends to help but the CPU is very easy including the highest difficulties.

Overall opinion: 

This game is far from the best Fifa (Fc), I wouldn't even say it's the best one in the last 5 years (Fifa 23 was better). However, this remains a step in the right direction and to be honest it is a very fun game. I just hope EA can do the following: 1) listen to their community (not advertising it only), 2) focus more on refining gameplay than graphics, 3) improve the ball physics in the air, 4) test their game before publishing it for the public :)

I also hope that they can stop the greedy corpo stuff they are doing (10 days early access, releasing the game with bug/glitches) and I hope they can take a year off and come back with fc28 being a drastically better experience.

To be able to even access the transfer market I had to play more than a dozen hours of mind numbing challenges in Ultimate Team (Which was the reason I bought the game in the first place). This immediately took it beyond the 2 hour steam refund window. Because the game was purchased within steam, the game is outside of EA's refund conditions, and because it took longer than 2 hours to unlock the content the game was purchased for, it fell significantly outside of steam's refund window.

The offline gameplay is reasonable, the game feels sluggish, but perhaps slightly more realistic than previous incarnations, but the heavily unrealistic dependence on pace abuse remains. The graphics are very pretty and the frame rate is decent for my system, which albeit is probably beyond recommended specs (RX7800xt)

The online game play is where the issues really begin to become untenable. There is a persistent input lag using default settings and any attempt to tweak them is short lived. The crossplay is NOT the culprit, as this input lag continues with it disabled. The extremely poor quality defensive controls mean that the speediest attackers are completely unplayable when combined with the obnoxiously unrealistic cut back animation, which does not pair well with the input lag. Whilst I'm clearly far from Top100 nowadays, I had a record of 100-4 at one point on FIFA 13 UT. Time hasn't been kind, but losing 11-2 and 9-2 in two consecutive games because of this input lag (Or worse, network manipulating opponents is probably beyond a skill issue)

The transfer market is a mess, with bots price fixing players as per usual, which makes the concept of timegating returning and new players to 48 hours before transfer activity completely redundant. Seeing players purchase players for multiple millions of coins, when it's brutally difficult to even afford 100k players when playing from scratch, signifies the sort of disparity in that regard. It might still be possible to grind to win on UT, but given, for example, a 24 team squad building challenge with 5 or 6 squads of 89 rated teams to be traded in to get a POTM Mbappe, when I had to spend forever bidding to try and get a washed Messi for under 10k, is a bad sign for me.

Seasons is at least reasonable, but the gameplay mechanics of cutbacks and wide pace spam still exist, but the input latency is significantly lower there than in UT somehow.

I honestly don’t care about Ultimate Team. I only play Career Mode anyway. That’s why I thought the game wouldn’t be so bad for me. However, the game feels absolutely unfinished. It’s on the level of an early access or demo. Career Mode is practically unplayable because of so many issues. Here are just a few:

- Players with homesickness never recover. They stay permanently unhappy, and every offer you get for them is handled by the assistant coach, meaning every deal falls through until the club withdraws the offer. You can’t sell them, you can’t renew their contract, and they stay unhappy which ruins their performance.

- Names sometimes just appear as code. Example: “Coach <!1> is in good form, let him play.”

- Sometimes Match results from other teams are all 0–0 (amazing).

- Players refuse to sign a contract extension with only 4 months left, and then later complain that they never got a new contract.

- Messages in general often don’t appear, whether from players, the board, or the assistant. As a result, you “ignore” them without even knowing it, which damages relationships and morale. For example, if a player doesn’t get a new contract in time, they’re automatically put on the transfer list, and then the assistant coach ruins the process again (Nice idea EA). 

- In many situations you simply can’t react to any message at all. you can only press “simulate” and move on.

- You’re spammed constantly with job offers as a manager. The assistant writes to you almost every day. In real life you could filter that out as spam or bulk delete it, but here you’re forced to simulate endless spam without any tools.

- Players sometimes don’t run for the ball. Both the AI and my own players just watch the ball roll.

- You randomly lose 50% of your transfer budget due to a “special event” and apparently never get it back.

- The board becomes dissatisfied with you and fires you even if you win 2 out of 3 titles (Before this i had an excellent standing).

- The so-called “special events” happen in clusters and the cluster is just the same event but spammed...

These are just some of the issues I constantly notice, and there are many more. Gameplay wise im not a good player, but  a good player would propably notice alot. The game is literally unplayable. I’ve never experienced EA FC this bad before (even though it is EA). And I’m usually someone who overlooks most bugs and doesn’t care much about them, since they dont impact my gameplay. But here it feels like driving a manual car with no clutch, no lights, no windows, and no steering wheel.

I would not recommend this game to anyone who mainly enjoys Career Mode. Oh, and the menu is completely broken too... it bugs out, has a life of its own, and is terribly confusing. Sadly, I can’t even get my money back, but you can definetly keep yours.

EA Sports FC 26 is a complete disappointment. If I had to rate the game overall, I would give it a 5/10 at best. But when it comes to the servers, it’s an absolute 0/10.

The servers do not reflect or support the global player base at all. They only serve players who are physically close to the data centers, leaving the majority of players—especially in regions like Asia, the Middle East, and Africa—with unbearable delay, lag, and unplayable matches.

I’ve experienced this issue already in FC-25, and now again in FC-26. Nothing has changed. The gameplay feels heavy, unresponsive, and unfair. The AI reacts faster than the human players, and competitive modes are ruined because of poor routing and terrible latency.

This is not just a minor issue—it is the core failure of the entire franchise. The management is failing the players, the server infrastructure is outdated, and EA has shown no serious effort to expand or optimize their global data centers. Right now, the servers are so bad that they wouldn’t even be enough to run a simple online game like Super Mario, let alone a “AAA competitive football title.”

EA needs a new management, new vision, and a complete rebuild of the server infrastructure from scratch. Until then, this franchise will remain broken, and millions of players will continue wasting their time and money on a game that is fundamentally unplayable outside of a few privileged regions.

FC26 Review – First Impressions After 15 Hours

After sinking 350+ hours in FC24 and FC25, I jumped into FC26 expecting a natural continuation. Instead, the game speed changes feel like a step backwards.

Authentic Mode – It’s painfully slow. Players move like they’re stuck in mud, passing feels delayed, and transitions lack urgency. Matches drag instead of flowing.

Competitive Mode – The complete opposite. Players run with godspeed as if the game turned into an arcade sprint fest. It looks unnatural and breaks immersion.

Balance Issue – The huge gap between Authentic and Competitive makes it hard to settle into a comfortable pace. Without using sliders (which I’m not a fan of), the experience feels forced and frustrating.

Gameplay Feel – Coming from FC25, where the balance of pace and flow was just right, FC26 feels disjointed. Even after 5 hours, I couldn’t adjust to either setting.

Verdict (Early Review):
FC26 is a letdown in terms of game speed and flow. Instead of evolving on FC25’s strengths, EA tinkered with something that didn’t need fixing. Unless a patch balances Authentic and Competitive, it’s hard to recommend this over FC25.

⭐ Rating (so far): 3/10 – Great visuals, same core gameplay, but ruined by speed imbalance.

Paid the extra to have the game early. Gameplay is a bit better than the previous version for sure but far from great. Worst thing is that it's so buggy. Among the weird things encountered constantly in the 17 hours I've played: (1) Random crash to desktop (2) Weird bug where it minimizes the game and brings you back to desktop (without crashing it) (3) Can't choose resolution (4) In career mode, despite creating my own manager or choosing an existing one, it always shows a random weird one in full kit.

Those are the bugs. Then I must say it has improved a bit in trying to cater for people who want realism instead of weird fantasy-like football with ridiculous skills, but not enough yet.

Things I would suggest: (1) Remove the exaggerated useless skill and add less fancy but more real movements with the right joystick, like a simple roll of the ball under the foot to evade someone. (2) Try and make shot styles, like the power shot, easier to use (so simpler button combinations). I get that there are some FIFA pros out there, but the random user wants to have fun and wants to be able to make realistic shots and passes without having to press 15 different buttons on a gamepad. (3) Keep improving AI and the sliders (expanded sliders are a big plus in this game). We want to have sliders but also an AI that has variation and flexibility depending on game situations and opponents. The CPU gameplay sliders are so important to make the game fun, but when you put them in custom, then there is no more variety. (4) For the love of God keep working on crosses and headers! Football players do actually place strong crosses into the box at various heights and players sometimes head them with power too!

It IS better than FC25 but still needs loads of work.

This is one off the best FIFA's {fc} in years.

I have played every FIFA game since FIFA 10. The gameplay is so much smoother, goalkeeper mistakes are few and far between and the AI awareness is, while still not perfect, a much bigger improvement on last year. I am mainly an UT player but play clubs / career mode here and there. There is so much more on offer in this FIFA than every other edition prior. With the addition off Tournaments, Silver Stars, Gaunlets, Live events, Live manager careers there is a game-mode for everyone. 

Also, a huge plus is the lowered power curve in this game. Its a lot more rewarding to grind and build your club this year than it has felt in any other game. Obvioulsy you still get the pay to win players, but it is relatively easy for you to build a club to a competitive level to compete with these players. 

I'm reading a lot off reviews that the game-play is laggy / slow / crashes and honestly that must be down to your PC. I haven't had a single issue with this game so far in that aspect. EA are not immune o bugs and there has been 1 or 2 issues with objectives tracking in UT, but other than that, not a single negative to say from their side. 

One last thing to add is that the games are very high scoring this year as defending is slightly harder than in other games, but that just makes you have to learn the mechanics to improve. If your looking to keep clean sheets every game, its definitely not for you. But it does make for a refreshing change that this game is fun, fast paced and more reliant on your control rather than AI movements. 

If you know your PC can handle it, and you have played the game before but are unsure if it is worth it, I promise it is. 1000% improvement on previous years.

Not sure why I fell for it again.

The gameplay is so far removed from realistic football these days, but not even in a fun way. I have mostly played Ultimate Team so my review will be mostly based on the gameplay from that game mode.

I will say Pro Clubs and Career Mode are okay, the game play seems more refined and enjoyable.

Back to Ultimate Team, the game play is terrible. 99% of the games end up with crazy score lines like 8-7, 9-8 etc.

It's super try hard. The spam passes, ping pong passing up and down the pitch is just annoying and unrealistic, think Tiki Taka but on steroids.

Defending is terrible, it's a manual defending system, but that means you must heavily rely on the defensive AI to properly position your other defenders and make basic interceptions etc. They do nothing, the defensive AI on this game is awful. 

Once players get the ball in the box, they just wiggle around a little with their player and the defensive AI will go completely brain dead and forget to track their man, intercept the ball or throw their body in the way of a simple shot. Same goes for short corners, they are broken, your defence just suddenly forgets how to do anything.

Finesse shots are nerfed so much that they may as well not be in the game. Low driven shots are the king. I feel like every game I play is the same, just against a different team in different kits. There is no variety to the game play, once the meta is established (that being all out attack and just outscore your opponents) then the game loses the fun aspect.

Pace is king, once again. If you have a CB with anything less than 78 pace, then you may as well just give up. Doesn't matter how strong they are. a 5'2" WSL striker with 65 strength manages to keep CB's with 90+ strength off the ball.

As you can imagine, UT is the same old gambling gateway that it's been for years. There's already a "Cornerstone" promotion after the game has been out to the general public for 1 day.

There are a lot of gameplay issues. Often times during a game, I pause and want to manage my team, the team management screen doesn't load at all. There is a severe bug with button delay/not registering your input whatsoever. I have had many occassions where I press the button to pass, and my player will just continue running as if I never pressed anything (this being in lobby's with 10-15ms ping) so not terrible connection which could be put down to lag.

Overall, the gameplay in UT is terrible. The game mode is a shallow gambling gateway designed to get people hooked onto buying FIFA points in hopes of landing that big player, or that new special promotional card.

If youi are buying the game solely for Career Mode or Clubs, I'd say it's worth a shot, but wait a few weeks for when this game is inevitably 30-50% cheaper.

Here’s a review + analysis of **EA Sports FC 26 (Steam / PC)** based on your experience (i5-13420H + RTX 4050 6 GB + 16 GB DDR5 + Gen4 SSD) plus community feedback — especially zooming in on the “massive FPS drops on corners / free kicks” issue you described.

---

## 🎮 First Impressions & Strengths

* The core gameplay (dribbling, passing, movement) can feel solid and responsive in “normal” match situations—when the camera is in standard positions and nothing dramatic is happening.
* Graphics / visual fidelity are decent, and with your hardware you have enough headroom to try medium–high settings.
* The game engine sometimes allows stable 50–100 FPS outside of set-piece transitions, which suggests your hardware is capable enough.

But that “outside of set pieces” caveat is crucial.

---

## ⚠️ Major Flaw: FPS Drops During Corners / Free Kicks / Cutscenes / Transitions

This is quite possibly **the biggest technical issue** in FC 26, especially on PC. Many players (including yourself) report that:

* When a corner, free kick, or set-piece sequence starts, the FPS tanks (sometimes to single digits or heavy stutter). ([EA Forums][1])
* The camera or view often transitions (from match view → set-piece view) and that seems to be a trigger for stuttering or freezing. ([Reddit][2])
* The drop can last across the duration of the set piece or a few seconds after. ([EA Forums][1])
* It’s not fixed by lowering all graphical settings — many report the same problem on low / medium / high / ultra. ([EA Forums][3])
* Some users claim it’s a shader compile issue or camera/cutscene transition overhead. ([Reddit][2])
* The problem has persisted through multiple EA / developer patches (i.e. community is still actively complaining). ([EA Forums][1])

So your observation (that the issue is present across all quality settings) matches what many others are seeing.

---

## 💻 Your System vs Expectations & Bottlenecks

Your setup:

* **CPU**: i5-13420H — a capable laptop CPU; decent single-core / mid-tier multi-core performance
* **GPU**: RTX 4050 (6 GB) — solid for 1080p / mid to high settings
* **Memory / SSD**: 16 GB DDR5 + Gen4 SSD — plenty fast and enough capacity

Given this, in “normal” match play your hardware should handle FC 26 comfortably (unless extremely high resolutions or uncanny settings). The fact that *set pieces* are triggering performance collapse suggests deeper problems beyond your GPU or CPU being underpowered.

Possible bottlenecks or culprits:

1. **Shader Compilation / Asset Streaming**

   * The camera switch / new view might be triggering sudden shader loads or asset streaming which the engine struggles to handle smoothly.
   * This would explain why even low settings don’t avoid the drop (because the drop is more about engine logic than raw graphical load).

2. **Poor Optimization / Engine Overheads**

   * EA’s engine might not fully be optimized for transitions/cutscenes, so even with good hardware you hit these weak points.
   * Code paths (like set-piece view rendering) may be less optimized / more CPU / memory bound.

3. **Memory Leaks / Frame Pacing Issues**

   * Over time, performance might degrade or stutter more — users have reported performance getting worse across matches. ([Hone][4])
   * Frame pacing problems where the game fails to sustain stable frame delivery, especially when transitions happen.

4. **Engine / Camera System Design**

   * The transitions themselves (camera repositioning, view changes, new lighting/shadows) could be inherently heavy in this version of the engine.
   * Possibly set-pieces use a different rendering path that is less optimized.

5. **Driver / API / Compatibility Issues**

   * Some issues might stem from GPU driver compatibility, or how the game engine uses DirectX / APIs / the driver.

---

## 🔍 What Works & What Doesn’t (Based on Community + Your Reports)

| Feature / Scenario                                 | What Works / Is Decent              | What Fails / Problematic                                |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Standard match play (no camera jumps)              | Often decent framerate / playable   | Occasional micro stutters                               |
| Camera transitions / cutscenes / set piece start   | Tends to be smooth until transition | Massive FPS drop, freeze, stutter                       |
| Running on different quality presets (low → ultra) | Visual fidelity changes             | The set piece issue remains                             |
| After playing for a while                          | Some stability                      | Potential performance degradation over time             |
| Online play / input / delay                        | Varies; some complaints             | Input lag, controller issues, delays during transitions |

Many users express frustration that even on high-end PCs the corners/free kicks stutter badly. ([Reddit][5])

---

## 🛠 Suggestions / Workarounds You Can Try

Since disabling / lowering all settings didn’t fix it, here are more targeted steps you can try. (I can help you test these if you want.)

1. **Cap FPS via GPU / Driver**

   * Rather than rely on in-game frame limits, use your NVIDIA control panel (or relevant GPU tool) to cap FPS (e.g. slightly below your monitor’s refresh).
   * Some community reports say capping at ~90 FPS helps stabilize performance and reduces stutter. ([Hone][4])

2. **Disable In-Game VSync / Use Driver VSync / G-Sync / FreeSync**

   * Avoid conflicting sync methods. Let the driver / monitor handle synchronization if possible. ([Reddit][2])

3. **Edit the FC Setup / Config File (fcsetup.ini)**

   * Force certain settings (disable some transitions, restrict render scaling, disable dynamic resolution) in the config file. ([Reddit][2])
   * Set the file to *Read Only* so the game doesn’t overwrite your tweaks. ([Reddit][2])

4. **Reduce Shader / Graphics Overhead**

   * Turn off advanced features like hair physics, cloth quality, ambient occlusion, dynamic shadows, etc.
   * Reduce render scale (i.e. internal resolution) to lighten load at transition moments.

5. **Restart Game / Avoid Long Sessions**

   * Because of memory leaks or performance degradation, restarting the game every few matches may help.

6. **Update GPU Drivers / Windows / Patches**

   * Make sure your GPU driver is latest version.
   * Keep the game patched. Sometimes fix updates reduce stuttering in transitions.

7. **Disable Overlays / Background Applications**

   * Steam Overlay, Discord overlay, etc., might add overhead during scene changes.

8. **Monitor Which Bottleneck Hits During Transition**

   * Use tools like MSI Afterburner (or RivaTuner) to monitor CPU / GPU / memory during transitions to see which drops first.

---

## 🧾 Final Verdict

EA Sports FC 26 is, in many respects, a decent football sim — but its major Achilles’ heel on PC right now is **absolutely the set-piece / camera transition performance collapse**. The fact that this occurs even on strong hardware (and is widely reported) suggests a core engine / optimization deficiency, not just “your PC is weak.”

For your system, the game should *have been* able to handle most parts well — and it does, except when corners / free kicks trigger that performance wipe. Because that issue undermines gameplay (set pieces are a fundamental part of matches), it severely impacts the experience.

If EA doesn’t patch or optimize these transitions, the game remains a frustrating experience on PC for many players.

After spending over 30 hours, I can confidently say this installment is a mixed bag at best. It has potential, but the issues are far too fundamental for me to recommend it.

One of the biggest problems is how heavily the outcome depends on latency. If you manage to secure extremely low latency, you essentially win 99% of the time, which makes the competitive aspect feel broken. On top of that, the game crashes frequently—most notably right after a penalty shootout ends. This has happened to me consistently, and it ruins the experience.

Defensive mechanics are poorly implemented, and the goalkeeper AI feels unreliable and weak, making matches frustrating for all the wrong reasons.

What makes this more disappointing is that I’m running the game on an RTX 4090 with a fiber optic connection. With such hardware and network conditions, I expected a smooth, optimized experience. Instead, it often feels like I’m not really in control of the match.

At this stage, I can’t recommend the game. However, once these issues are fixed and the gameplay feels right, I will gladly change my review to a positive one.

I went into FC 26 hoping for even one thing that would make it feel fresh. After testing the game, it hit me: this is last year’s game wearing a new shirt. The same animation lock-ins still swallow your inputs. Defenders still snap into “magnetic” tackles. Refereeing still flips from blind to nitpicky. And the AI still swings between ball-watching and psychic. It’s all very familiar, in the worst way.

Ultimate Team? Same narrow meta: pace, press, cutbacks. You’re funneled into the exact builds that worked last year because defensive recovery, collisions, and shooting assistance haven’t truly changed. The grind-to-compete loop is intact, and the store whispers the same old answer: pay up. Career Mode and Clubs get UI shuffles and a few knobs turned, but the way you actually play, progress, and plan seasons is untouched. Busywork, not innovation.

What really breaks the spell is the technical déjà vu. Menu lag is back. Matchmaking still feels flaky. Replays stutter in the same spots. Haptics are inconsistent. Even little camera snaps pop up like ghosts you thought were exorcised. If you wrote down a list of last year’s annoyances, you can pretty much check them off again.

Here’s the simple, solid test I use for any full-price sequel: does it add a new core system, deliver a real overhaul of something major, or bring meaningful content that obviously couldn’t just be a season update? FC 26 doesn’t clear any of those bars. That’s not “taste”, that’s a value check. If the changes boil down to tuning sliders, minor UI tweaks, and content rotations, that’s a patch, not a new game.

So I asked for a refund. And I’m done funding this cycle, EA won’t see my money again. If you own last year’s FC, you already have this one in everything that counts. I don’t recommend FC 26 to anyone. Save your cash and your patience.

I’ve always thought EA FC gets misleading review scores on Steam because of its heavy Ultimate Team focus and yearly release cycle. After sinking 11 hours into career mode, though, my takeaway is unfortunately negative.

The gameplay itself is fantastic. My very first match was an exhibition between Barcelona and Real Madrid, and it was the best game of EA FC/FIFA I’ve played in years—tactical, fluid, and genuinely enjoyable.

For career mode, I started with Melbourne Victory since I wanted to do a manager journey. It seemed more manager-focused this year with the manager market, and while the players felt worse due to being less skilled, that was fine—it added authenticity, and I still enjoyed the matches.

But the career mode itself? Absolutely awful. I dread advancing between games because every time I do, a player asks for more money and I get five transfer offers for someone I literally just gave a new contract to. The board randomly drops my job security to “okay,” even though my only two objectives are “win the league” and “make the playoffs”—and I’m top, 10 points clear with eight games left.

Not to mention, for the first time ever I’m experiencing major screen tearing and graphical glitches, along with gameplay bugs like the AI constantly shooting from insanely far out. These are issues I’ve never encountered in previous entries, which makes them even more frustrating.

The in-game commentary is terrible too. Commentators constantly misgender players, referring to women transfers as “he,” and they’ll say things like “Auckland fans love Steve Corica,” even though in my save Auckland is dead last with just two wins. Little immersion-breaking details like this stack up quickly. Press conferences are still bad and basically pointless.

At this point, I only play player career mode each year because it’s the most stable option (though it still has major flaws). I dabble in Ultimate Team, but even that feels like the same recycled startup every year. The whole series feels tired, like the devs don’t actually play career mode themselves—they just keep piling on new features over a shaky foundation, leaving it clunky, cluttered, and unimmersive. I end up skipping every transfer cutscene, pre-match activity, and press conference just to get through it.

Anyway, enough rambling—let’s hope FM 26 delivers. 🙏

I’ve sunk around 26 hours into this game since Early Access dropped on Friday, and honestly, I regret wasting my time. In its current state, this game is an absolute mess and I cannot recommend it to anyone.

The online gameplay is borderline unplayable. Every single match has massive controller delay — your inputs feel like they’re going through mud. Half the time, your player will keep running straight off the pitch or just hand the ball to the opposition because the game can’t keep up. It doesn’t feel competitive, it feels broken.

Performance is even worse. Every FUT match starts out somewhat stable, but as soon as the second half begins, the FPS nosedives to single digits (5–10 FPS). Imagine trying to play an online match where the screen stutters and freezes every time you touch the ball. It’s impossible to enjoy, let alone win.

And then there’s the latency. Some games spike so badly that your ping shoots up to 500–1000+. At that point you’re not even playing football, you’re watching a slideshow while your opponent walks the ball into the net. For a full-priced sports title in 2025, this level of network stability and optimization is unacceptable.

Defending in this game is a nightmare, and I hardly played the previous one because of this change in mechanics. It should reward players who attack in the right way, not those who abuse zigzags. Similarly, it should reward players who defend well and not punish them for the slightest mistake, but we find EA's signature touch in the tackle success rate and the probability of getting good players in packs. The same goes for covering deep passes, which is completely non-existent. In my opinion, they should improve defence against deep runs and defender mobility to block techniques (or slow down techniques so that they are less difficult to defend against, especially against agile players who manage to sneak through).

Poor positioning of attacking players in possession play, where players tend to stand in a line and wait around pointlessly. The keeper is improved in all other cases except this particular one. Not to mention the mechanics of being able to move the goalkeeper, which, I think, is an exploit.

Moreover, with these new mechanics, the games are draining and exhausting because they require too much concentration. I preferred the old ones, where there were fewer goals and which, to me, were more like football. I also felt more proud after a match than I do now, where there are goals everywhere and performing a technical move was proof of talent and not just something to tick off to make the whole thing easier.

I'm starting to enjoy playing against bots more than against other players. It should be a good game for solo players to at least play a real game of football. And I'm excited to try out the authentic mode, which I hope will give me hope to enjoy FC again.

Finally, EA is putting effort into the content, as it is one of the biggest football games on the market, and continues to add interesting features to both career mode and other game modes. A season pass with rewards mixed between solo and UT content. I could understand it for UT players, but for solo players, it's really a questionable choice. Furthermore, evolutions are a feature that I find underused, because you want to upgrade your ‘favourite’ players, but most of them disappear after a while or cannot be reused. What's more, you're still stuck in a co-op menu when playing with a friend. You just have to wait for them to start a match, and you can't do anything, not even watch their team.

In conclusion, only buy FC26 if you agree with these new mechanics and do your research before purchasing this game. I would advise waiting for a good discount, given that the quality on PC is still below that of consoles, and if you are looking for a recent football game to play with friends. For my part, I'm waiting for a potential upgrade on the points I mentioned above. If nothing happens, unfortunately, I'll feel like I've been ripped off and will think twice before buying an FC game at full price.

But first, let’s start with the positives:

The PC version works great! Finally! After years of awful PC ports, we finally have a performant PC version that actually works really well.

EA FC 26 is definitely a step in the right direction compared to the last few entries. Gameplay feels smoother, animations are cleaner, and player movement finally has that bit of responsiveness fans have been asking for. It’s fair to say this is the best the series has felt in the past 3–4 years — but let’s be honest, that’s not exactly a high bar to clear. The previous games were absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in terms of consistency, realism, and overall fun, so calling this one “the best in years” doesn’t mean it’s suddenly great — just less broken.

That said, the same old frustrations still hang around. There are still those matches where it genuinely feels like the game is out to get you — rebounds falling perfectly to your opponent, passes going completely off target for no reason, or sudden momentum swings that make you wonder if your input even matters. It’s hard to stay engaged when it feels like the game decides who wins before kickoff.

And to make things worse, the same technical issues from past years are still here. Crashes still happen — sometimes in menus, sometimes right as you’re loading into a match — and when they do, you get slapped with a DNF (Did Not Finish) as if you quit on purpose. On top of that, the game punishes you by cutting down the coins you earn in your next matches. That penalty doesn’t just go away either — it snowballs. Once you’re hit with it, you’re stuck earning reduced rewards basically for the rest of your time playing until the next EA FC comes out. It’s ridiculous and unfair, especially when the crash wasn’t even your fault.

When everything’s working properly, EA FC 26 shows glimpses of what the series could be — skill-based, smooth, and rewarding. But between the questionable scripting, lingering bugs, and unfair penalties, it’s still a long way from being the game fans deserve.

The controller issue is fixed, but only to be replaced with a similar issue in which the game would be completely unplayable with horrible framerate and delay, and the ONLY fix I could find online and through EA support was to play 60hz 60fps with vsync on. - framerate drops for a few seconds after kick off

-sometimes experienced significant framerate lag and delay when opening a pack

These are all purely performance issues that can be avoided by just playing on console. I haven't even talked about how the game kinda just sucks in general. After the honeymoon phase, and enough time past for people to figure out how to abuse the game mechanics, it quickly became apparent that the game is severely flawed:

-significantly more likely to score or concede straight after kickoff no matter what skill level you are (I watch Bugs on twitch who is a very good player and the majority of goals are from kickoff. He had a game that finished 10-9 recently. That's not an exaggeration.)

-having a better team than your opponent is the most relevant it has ever been: I'm very experienced with the franchise and know how to build a solid team on an RTG with meta players and good playstyles and stats. I've balled out with the likes of Inaki and Nico Williams, Ayoze Perez, hell even Lewandowski and Sam Kerr have proven to me that they can compete, but the problem is that they are so unbelievably gapped by the meta attackers (looking at you Claudia Pina, Mbappe and Dembele). The team diff is most obvious in draft, where even if you have a solid team with fast and capable players and a good goalkeeper, you pretty much just auto lose if you match an opponent with R9, Ronaldinho and Mbappe even if they are about the same skill level (I know from first-hand experience. In previous FIFAs I'd say that having a slightly better team was negligible, if not borderline irrelevant. In those games I could still win the game if I just played better. Even when coming up against a full meta credit card icon squad, the game was still competitive with an RTG squad. This year however, you are actually at a decent disadvantage with a B tier squad versing an A tier squad, which will only encourage people to spend hundreds and give this stupid billion dollar company even more money in hopes they can have some hope of competing.

-the majority of the goals you concede leave you with more questions than answers, such as: "why couldn't I player switch to that defender? Why didn't my goalkeeper save that even though I moved them the right way? How do I tackle his Claudia Pina who has turned into a fidget spinner? Why is my Inaki Williams unable to catch up to my opponent's gold Rabiot who is currently running with the ball on a counter attack from a corner? Where is my defence? How has Rabiot not been caught yet? Why is there no one in the box to stop this free cross to his striker? What is Rabiot's pace?" 
I only remember saying "that was a good goal, he got me there" once in my most recent champs games. In previous titles I could clearly recognise where I had misplayed, or where I had been completely outplayed, but it rarely happens this year. Even if I do get "outplayed" it's because my opp wiggled and passed his way around my defence who seem to be sleep walking.

-on the flipside, attacking isn't very rewarding. It's nearly impossible to score from outside the box, even with precision shooting, so you're forced to play ping pong with your midfielders and attackers until you inevitably get an opening to pass, turn and correctly guess which way your opp is moving their keeper to go the opposite way, or you just hit a low driven if they don't move. I decided to buy EAFC26 as they promised better gameplay on top of icons in career mode. I usually only buy Fifa once every 3 years, but this is my 3rd year in a row due to CL changes.

The main reason I am downvoting this game, is because the AI on World-class level is insanely OP compared to prior titles.
I play with my own created club Macclesfield in the 4th division of the UK.
The issue I have, is that my players have the fysical turning circle  as big as a Boeing 747, whereas the AI has small turning circles.  (Whilst they all have the same stats!)

The AI also knows exactly your input, and responds before your players do anything, on your input.  Their reaction time and anticipating on *simulated* is unhuman and faster than you can ever anticipate; this is significantly idiotic and not realistic at all, it rather is unrealistic and feels more like you are learning to fool the AI rather than play football.

Also MBappe is slower on ball than Robin Pröpper with pace 36 running after him if you are the one controlling MBappe; the AI is just stupidly faster than you are and controls the ball 2 times as well as you do, even if you have the same stats for you and AI on PC.

The AI also feels unbalanced in tactics;  your players are 10 clueless clowns watching the opponent do whatever they want even if you have made pressing tactics and role tactics, whilst the CPU AI perfectly runs into open spaces and is constantly moving.

Take note I only play career and on world-class difficulty.

The second part I feel scammed about, is that Icons are only available in career in a specific gamemodel, and you cannot create your own club and add icons, or have them on the market in your game.   This is a missed shot as I would have liked to build up my own club and eventually buy icons to use them.

The positive note I will put is that playing, if you get to play football feels a lot more rewarding and nicer when you score a goal, the passing and shooting also looks more realistic in itself.

Precision passing and Input (random passes to narnia) are still ass, but EA hasn't been able to fix that for 3 years in a row now so that should be considered a ''feature'' at this point.

Ea has done it again though, promised a lot and advertised it as something amazing baiting many people into buying it, but in the end it's another broken, unbalanced game.

EDIT: with recent updates they made the AI even more OP for the opponent and your own AI is still useless. They should be sued for false advertising and scamming.

Overall, FC 26 is a strong entry that offers fun and challenging gameplay, but passing still needs refinement to reach the level of consistency fans expect.

I’ve been playing this game since 2009, and over the past half-decade or so, it has consistently and progressively deteriorated. Like a lot of players out there, I am, for the first time in a while, having fun playing this game. Make no mistake, we are not back to the golden age of FIFA, but this is significantly more enjoyable than that slop we have had for the last few years, probably since FIFA 17, and definitely since FIFA 23. 

I’ll start with the positives, the first being the most essential thing: the gameplay. The gameplay this year feels very smooth. Passing in this game is nothing short of phenomenal, and it has actually helped to make so many formations more usable for that tiki-taka type of playstyle. Defending has finally been nerfed, which I would also say has been a huge net positive for the game. The days of letting the AI do all you’re defending while roaming around with your CDM are seemingly gone, and I hope it stays that way. To compensate for the heavily nerfed defending, though, goalkeepers are extremely overpowered in my opinion. However, I am not against that, given how many overpowered shooting playstyles there are in the game, such as finesse and low-driven shots. I have just started using precision shooting this year, and I can already see that it is the best option for shooting with the way the gameplay is this year. Scoring goals is no longer just about having the fastest players with the most overpowered shooting styles. It’s also about timing your shots correctly and taking control of your aim. These factors, in addition to defending and the slower power curve, reward players with skill, which is excellent. There is also noticeably less of a “meta” in this game. Having the fastest players is still the go-to option, but it is no longer as necessary as it was in the past few years. If you have the skill, you will destroy opponents who essentially don’t know what they’re doing, and just have pace on their side, and that’s a good thing. The game rewards you for being good, which is something that has not been present in this franchise for the past few years. EA also appears to be listening to the fanbase, at least over the past few months, and has already implemented fast and effective changes requested by the community. Hopefully, they will continue to do so.

Overall, the game is in the best shape it has been in for at least the past three years, perhaps longer. Will it stay that way? There’s no way to know. It’s been a long time since long-time players of this franchise have been able to enjoy this game once again. Hopefully, despite the high unlikelihood of it happening, the franchise will continue to improve.

Generally speaking, I am a big fan of most FC/FIFA games, but I cannot recommend you to buy this on PC until they fix a few issues:

First of all, there is an issue where the game forces you to play with keyboard and mouse at times, which is incredibly frustrating in a game series where the only real option is to play with a controller, something I have been doing for 20 years at this point. In important online games, it was not possible to switch the controls back to my dualsense controller which worked perfectly fine in the menus. This needs a fix before I will ever consider buying this game on PC.

Also, this was my first time trying to buy a FC/FIFA game on PC, and I was really looking forward to it (good graphics and low latency goes brrrrr). Sadly, my experience was ruined by having to grind squad battles and other boring modes for hours before being able to purchase players off the transfer market in Ultimate Team. This meant that I basically had to open packs which cost me even more money to get any players I didn't mind having in my team. If I were to continue playing this game in an attempt to 'unlock' the transfer market, I would also have to waste an evolution on a random player I got in a pack, instead of using it on a player I actually would have in my team for more than a day or two. This system of verification or whatever is terrible, and completely ruins the first experience players have with this game on PC. 

If you have played FC games on PC or through Steam before, I suppose this shouldn't be a problem for you... but it still ruined my first experience with the game along with controller issues, which is why I asked for a refund. I hope these issues get resolved, but until then I cannot recommend getting this game on PC.

No matter what I understand that I am the clown. I keep buying this game, I keep giving you money, and I am equally hopeful every single year that it will be different. It rarely, if ever, is. And again, there has been an absolute disaster of a launch for us on PC. Game won't start, it crashes, it requires you to verify your product, took a few hours before the game even launched, and when it did launch it was FULL of User Interface bugs. I only play Career Mode so I can't speak for Ultimate Team players, however there are more bugs in Career Mode than I could care to explain here. Some of the "old but gold" ones include not being able to see the amount you are offering another club for a player because the numbers blend in with the white cinematic background that they have been recycling for 5 years now. Another "small"--small details matter just as much as big ones, if not more, especially when it comes to immersion and realism--visual nuisance is the fact that if your created manager now wears a shirt, during rainy games, he won't put on a jacket, something EA has had in their game for as long as I can remember. How is stuff like this even remotely possible? How does it get worse? How does it get MORE buggy? How does it remove tiny details we have already had in the game for a decade? It's mind boggling to me. As of right now there are still only 7 subs on the bench in the Premier League. There is also literally zero sound in-game. I have tried to reinstall, verify game-files, still nothing. Still no sound, no commentary. I remember this being an issue in past games as well. Sigh. 

One thing I will give EA is that the teams have launched with their 3rd kits this year. Everton got the new stadium too, without us having to wait 5 Title Updates before getting it/them. This should just be the norm, but last iterations haven't always launched with the new stadiums and 3rd kits. This time it did. 

It goes from funny to sad when you look into how much money you make as a company, and yet you keep taking advantage of us. At the VERY LEAST you could have given us a game that actually plays, that actually works... but no, you keep delivering this buggy mess every year. And I get it, I am the idiot for buying it. But I love football and sadly there are no other competitors for it. So I keep coming back like a guy to his abusive, toxic ex-girlfriend with a fat booty.
